articles.title: झापाका ४२ परिवार तनावमा, अन्तिम किस्ता रोकिएपछि छटपटि
articles.summary:
झापा । झापाको मेचीनगरस्थित दिपज्योती टोलका ४२ परिवार दुई दशकअघि किस्ताबन्दीमा खरिद गरेको जग्गाको लालपूर्जा नपाउँदा समस्यामा परेका छन् । मेचीनगर २ र ३ को सिमानास्थित जग्गा हालसम्म नामसारी हुन नसक्दा पीडित परिवारको समस्या झन् जटिल बन्दै गएको छ ।

झापाको मेचीनगर ३ स्थित बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहेको चिया बगान नभएको खाली जग्गा वि.स २०६३÷०६४ सालमा शुभ चिया प्रालिले बैना गरि घरघडेरीका लागि स्थानीयलाई किस्ताबन्दी एकदेखि पाँच कठ्ठासम्म बिक्री प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढायो ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारलाई लक्षित गरी बिक्री गरिएको उक्त जग्गाको अधिकांश किस्ता तिरे पनि अन्तिम किस्ता लिएपछि लालपूर्जा उपलब्ध गराउने सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएको पीडितहरूको भनाइ छ ।

अन्तिम किस्ता पनि तिर्न तयार भएका उनीहरुको संस्थाले रकम नै लिएन । अहिले उनीहरुको न पैसा फिर्ता भएको छ, न लालपूर्जा नै पाएका छन् ।

त्यस्तै पीडित स्थानीयका अनुसार जग्गा बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहे पनि तत्कालीन शुभ चिया प्रालिका अध्यक्ष हेमराज भारतीले कारोबार अगाडी बढाएका थिए । तर उनले पैसा लिएपछि त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न आलटाल गरेको दुखेसो पीडित पोख्छन् । उनीहरुले जग्गा समस्या तत्काल समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

यता शुभ चिया प्रालिका वर्तमान अध्यक्ष रमेश दाहालले विगतमा कारोबार संस्थागत प्रक्रियाअनुसार नभएकाले समस्या उत्पन्न भएको बताउँछन् । समस्या समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायसँग आवश्यक गृहकार्य भइरहेको र पीडितलाई न्याय दिलाउने प्रयास जारी रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारले साहुसंग ऋण गरेर किस्ता वापतको रकम समेत दिइ सकेको अवस्थामा अन्तिम किस्ता नलिई जग्गाको स्वामित्व समेत प्रदान नगर्दा ४२ परिवार समस्यामा परेका छन् । तसर्थ उनीहरुलाई सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायले यथाशिघ्र समस्या समाधान गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: नेपाल लाइफको ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान, १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा आर्जन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालको सर्वाधिक विश्वासिलो जीवन बीमा कम्पनीका रूपमा स्थापित नेपाल लाइफ इन्स्योरेन्सले आफ्नो २५ वर्षको गौरवमय यात्रा (सिल्भर जुबिली) का अवसरमा रु. १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा शुल्क (FPI) आर्जन गर्दै जीवन बीमा इतिहासमा नयाँ ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान कायम गरेको छ।

गत आर्थिक वर्षमा रु. १० अर्ब प्रथम बीमा शुल्क आर्जन गरेको कम्पनीले यस वर्ष उक्त उपलब्धिलाई अझ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउँदै बीमा उद्योगमा नयाँ मानक स्थापित गरेको हो।

यस ऐतिहासिक सफलताका अवसरमा कम्पनीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रमण पराजुलीले सम्पूर्ण बीमित, अभिकर्ता, कर्मचारी, शेयरधनी तथा सरोकारवालाहरू प्रति आभार व्यक्त गर्दै आगामी दिनमा अझ थप प्रविधिमैत्री सेवा, नवीन बीमा योजना र उत्कृष्ट सेवा प्रदान गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे ।

articles.title: सिद्धार्थ बैंकद्वारा ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सुविधा सञ्चालनमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सिद्धार्थ बैंक लिमिटेडले ग्राहकहरुको तत्कालको वित्तीय आवश्यकतालाई सहज र सर्वसुलभ बनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ नयाँ कर्जा योजना ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

यस योजना अन्तर्गत ग्राहकहरुले आफ्नो सुन तथा सुनका गरगहनाहरु धितो राखी बैंकबाट अधिकतम रु. ५० लाखसम्मको कर्जा रकम प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्, जसमा धितो सुनको मूल्यांकनका आधारमा बढीमा ७५ प्रतिशतसम्म कर्जा प्रवाह गरिनेछ।

ग्राहकहरूले आफ्नो व्यक्तिगत तथा व्यावसायिक आवश्यकता सहज रूपमा पूरा गर्न सकुन् भन्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको यो सुरक्षित र भरपर्दो सुविधा हालका लागि बैंकको काठमाडौंस्थित न्यूरोड गेट शाखाबाट उपलब्ध छ, र यस सम्बन्धी थप जानकारीका लागि बैंकको २४ सै घण्टा सञ्चालनमा रहने ग्राहक सेवा केन्द्र ‘सिद्धार्थ केयर’ मा सम्पर्क गर्न सकिनेछ।

articles.title: कतारमा नेपाली समुदायद्वारा स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली
articles.summary:
कतार । गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) राष्ट्रिय समन्वय परिषद् (एनसीसी) कतारले स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस फादर अमिर शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्न शोकसभा आयोजना गरेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व तथा कतारको समृद्धि, विकास र विश्वमञ्चमा स्थापित गराउन पुर्‍याएको अतुलनीय योगदानको उच्च सम्मान गरिएको थियो।

कार्यक्रममा कतारस्थित नेपाली राजदूतावासका कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेल प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी भएका थिए। साथै कतारमा क्रियाशील विभिन्न नेपाली सामाजिक तथा कल्याणकारी संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेखनीय उपस्थिति रहेको थियो। शोकको यस घडीमा नेपाली समुदायले एकता र ऐक्यबद्धता प्रदर्शन गरेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रमको सुरुआत पवित्र कुरआनको तिलावतबाट भएको थियो भने मौलाना गुलाम नबी रजबीले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको आत्माको चिरशान्तिको कामना गर्दै कतार राज्यको शान्ति, स्थायित्व र समृद्धिका लागि विशेष दुआ गरेका थिए।

एनआरएनए एनसीसी कतारका अध्यक्ष कृष्ण पन्थीले स्वागत मन्तव्य दिँदै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको निधनप्रति गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गरे।

उनले कतारका अमिर, राजपरिवार, सरकार तथा सम्पूर्ण कतारी जनताप्रति समवेदना व्यक्त गर्दै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व, राष्ट्र निर्माणमा खेलेको ऐतिहासिक भूमिका र उनले छोडेको प्रेरणादायी विरासतको प्रशंसा गरे। पन्थीले कतारलाई विश्वकै सम्मानित र समृद्ध राष्ट्रका रूपमा स्थापित गर्न फादर अमिरको योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहेको बताए।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख वक्ता प्राध्यापक मोहम्मद रमजान अली मियाँले नेपाल–कतारबीचको लामो समयदेखिको मित्रवत सम्बन्ध र बढ्दो सहकार्यबारे चर्चा गरे। उनले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको नेतृत्वमा कतारले आर्थिक विविधीकरण, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, पूर्वाधार विकास तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कूटनीतिमा उल्लेखनीय प्रगति हासिल गरेको बताए। साथै कतारले हजारौँ नेपालीलाई रोजगारी तथा अवसर उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे।

कतारस्थित नेपाली दूतावासका तर्फबाट बोल्दै कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेलले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै उनको योगदानको उच्च प्रशंसा गरे।

उनले नेपाल–कतारबीचको मैत्रीपूर्ण सम्बन्ध निरन्तर सुदृढ हुँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै आगामी दिनमा दुई देशबीचको सहयोग र मित्रतालाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी विभिन्न नेपाली संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले पनि शोक मन्तव्य व्यक्त गर्दै कतारले नेपाली समुदायलाई प्रदान गरेको अवसरप्रति आभार प्रकट गरे। साथै कठिन घडीमा कतारका नेतृत्व र जनताप्रति ऐक्यबद्धता तथा सम्मान व्यक्त गरे।

श्रद्धाञ्जली सभा अन्त्यमा स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीको सम्मानमा सामूहिक प्रार्थना तथा एक मिनेट मौनधारण गरिएको थियो। कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व र योगदानले आगामी पुस्तालाई पनि प्रेरणा दिइरहने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका थिए।

articles.title: मिटर ब्याज पीडितलाई मनाउन सुधनको कसरत, बल्ल माने पीडित
articles.summary:
बारा । बाराको निजगढ नगरपालिका–८ स्थित निजगढ नगर उद्योग वाणिज्य संघको सभाहलमा तीन दिनदेखि जारी सरकार र मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलनको निर्णायक वार्ता अब राजधानी काठमाडौंमा हुने भएको छ । मिटरब्याज पीडित सरकारसँग वार्ता गर्न जहाजबाट काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

जनकपुरबाट काठमाडौंतर्फ पैदल न्याय मार्चमा रहेका मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूसँग गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले बुधबार करिब पाँच घण्टा लामो छलफल गरेका थिए । छलफलका क्रममा आन्दोलनकारीहरूले उठाएका छ बुँदे मागबारे विस्तृत रूपमा कुराकानी भएको थियो ।

आन्दोलन पक्षका अनुसार सरकारले उनीहरूले अघि सारेका सम्पूर्ण माग कार्यान्वयन गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ । बुधबार राति निष्कर्षविहीन बनेको वार्तापछि नेपाल सरकारका गृहमन्त्री सुदन गुरुङले आन्दोलनकारीलाई वार्ता टोली गठन गरी सिंहदरबारस्थित गृह मन्त्रालयमा आउन आग्रह गरेका थिए ।

वार्ताका क्रममा गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले सहमतिपत्रमा रहेका केही शब्द तथा भाषागत विषयमा संशोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको बताएका थिए । कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक पक्षसमेत मिलाउनुपर्ने भएकाले तत्काल हस्ताक्षर गर्नु उपयुक्त नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो ।

त्यसपछि गृहमन्त्रीको पटक–पटकको आग्रह र आन्दोलनकारी पक्षको आन्तरिक छलफलपछि मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालले पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोली गठन गरी बिहीबार काठमाडौं प्रस्थान गरेको हो । अन्य आन्दोलनकारी भने वार्ताको नतिजा नआएसम्म बाराको निजगढमै रहने जनाइएको छ ।

काठमाडौं प्रस्थान आएको पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोलीको संयोजकमा केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहा रहेका छन् । टोलीमा केन्द्रीय महासचिव मनोज कुमार पासवान, केन्द्रीय प्रवक्ता रिजन राना मगर, केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य लक्ष्मी घिमिरे तथा केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य किरण परियार सदस्य रहेका छन् । वार्ता टोलीको रोहबरमा संयुक्त जनअधिकार मोर्चाका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष निर्ग नवीन लगायतका प्रतिनिधिहरू पनि काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

आन्दोलनका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहाले सरकारले माग पूरा गर्न सकारात्मक प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको भए पनि त्यसलाई कानुनी रूपमा स्पष्ट र लिखित रूपमा सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने बताए ।

उनले आन्दोलनकारीको उद्देश्य सहमतिपत्रमा हस्ताक्षर मात्र नभई त्यसको प्रभावकारी कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित गर्नु रहेको उल््लेख गर्दै वार्ता सकारात्मक निष्कर्षमा पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: कांग्रेस नेता अभिषेक गिरीको अपराध साम्राज्य !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ‘हिजो गल्ती भयो, अब समाजसेवामा लाग्छु’ भनी करिब तीन वर्षअघि कारागारबाट छुट्दा अभिषेक गिरीले दिएको सन्देशले धेरैलाई उनी बदलिएको विश्वास दिलाएको थियो । तर, समाजसेवाको आवरणमा पुरानै आपराधिक सञ्जाल सञ्चालन गरेको आरोपमा अहिले उनी फेरि प्रहरी नियन्त्रणमा छन् । मोरङ प्रहरी र केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सीआईबी) दुवैले उनीविरुद्ध ठगी र आपराधिक विश्वासघातसम्बन्धी उजुरीमाथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेका छन् ।

२०७९ चैत ५ गते नौ वर्ष जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेर कारागारबाट निस्कँदा अभिषेक गिरी साधु भएको आभाष दिलाएका थिए । विगतका गल्ती नदोहो¥याउने प्रतिवद्धता जनाउँदै उनले समाजसेवामा समर्पित हुने घोषणा गरेका थिए ।

त्यसपछि उनले ‘गिरी फाउन्डेसन’ स्थापना गरे, सामाजिक कार्यक्रममा सक्रिय देखिए र आर्थिक रूपमा विपन्नलाई सहयोग गर्न थाले । तर, प्रहरी अनुसन्धानले अभिषेक समाजसेवाको आडमा आपराधिक क्रियाकलापमा संलग्न रहेको भन्दै गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

गिरीमाथि लागेको आरोप के हो ?

अहिले सीआईबीले अनुसन्धानका लागि मोरङबाट काठमाडौं ल्याएका गिरीलाई यसअघि जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय मोरङले पक्राउ गरेको थियो । उनी पक्राउ परेको विषय पनि निकै रोचक छ । कारागार बाहिरका मान्छेको कारागारभित्र कुनै पहुँच हुँदैन ।

कुनै कैदीबन्दीलाई भेट्न जानु प¥यो भने पनि भेटघाटको कारण खुलाउँदै प्रशासनको अनुमति लिएर सुरक्षा जाँच पार गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ । अझ कारागारभित्रको प्रशासनको बाहिर कुनै साइनो नै हुँदैन । यति सुरक्षित रहने कारागारको शासन भने गिरीले बाहिरै बसेर चलाउँथे ।

कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्तामा समेत कब्जा जमाएर असुल्ने गरेको भन्दै गिरीविरुद्ध कैदीबन्दीले नै आवाज उठाएका थिए ।

कैदीबन्दीले बनाएको मुढा र गलैँचाको पैसा गिरीले बुझ्ने गरेको आरोप छ । असार १२ गते कैदीबन्दीलाई बाँडेको १३ लाख ४० हजार रुपैयाँ असुल गरेको आरोप पनि गिरीमाथि छ ।

कारागारभित्रको खाद्यान्न र तरकारी आपूर्तिमा समेत उनको सिन्डिकेट चल्ने गरेको कैदीबन्दीको गुनासो थियो । प्रहरीका अनुसार, गिरीमाथि अहिले दुई फरक प्रकृतिका आरोपमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ ।

मोरङमा कारागारभित्र हुने आर्थिक गतिविधिमा बाहिरबाट प्रभाव पार्दै कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्ता, उनीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका सामग्रीको रकम तथा आपूर्ति व्यवस्थामा अवैध हस्तक्षेप गरेको आरोपका आधारमा असार १३ गते मोरङ प्रहरीले उनलाई पक्राउ गरेको हो । उनको घरमा गरिएको खानतलासीका क्रममा नगद गन्ने मेसिनसमेत फेला परेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ ।

उच्च अदालत विराटनगरको आदेशपछि उनी मोरङबाट छुटे पनि त्यही दिन सीआईबीले पुनः नियन्त्रणमा लियो । यसपटक भने निर्माण व्यवसायी सुवास श्रेष्ठको उजुरीका आधारमा अनुसन्धान अघि बढाइएको छ ।

पहुँचका आधारमा ठेक्का दिलाइदिने आश्वासन दिएर ठगी गरेको, निर्माण उपकरण नियन्त्रणमा लिएको तथा जबर्जस्ती सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण गराएको आरोपमा आपराधिक विश्वासघात र ठगीसम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान भइरहेको सीआईबीको भनाइ छ । प्रहरीले घटनासँग सम्बन्धित प्रमाण संकलन र बयान लिने काम जारी रहेको जनाएको छ ।

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि भने लामो छ । प्रहरीको अभिलेखअनुसार उनी पहिलो पटक २०५८ सालमा पक्राउ परेका थिए । त्यसयता कुटपिट, सार्वजनिक अपराध, डाँका चोरी, ज्यान मार्ने उद्योग र अन्ततः अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धकजस्ता विभिन्न मुद्दामा उनी ११ पटकसम्म पक्राउ परिसकेका छन् ।

२०७१ सालमा अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धक मुद्दामा दोषी ठहर भएपछि उनले लामो जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेका थिए । कारागारबाट छुटेपछि उनी सामाजिक र राजनीतिक गतिविधिमा समेत सक्रिय बने । तर, पछिल्ला घटनाक्रमले उनको पुनः आपराधिक गतिविधिसँग सम्बन्ध रहेको आरोपलाई प्रहरीले गम्भीर रूपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अझै जारी रहेकाले उनीमाथि लागेको आरोप अदालतबाट प्रमाणित भइसकेको अवस्था भने होइन । अब प्रहरी अनुसन्धान र अदालतको अन्तिम निर्णयले अभिषेक गिरीको कर्तुतको नयाँ पर्दाफास हुनेछ ।

articles.title: अपरेसन चार्लीबाट खुलेको रहस्य, नक्कली नोट छाप्ने गिरोह पक्राउ
articles.summary:
रुपन्देही । रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नेपाली नोट, नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गरिएका उपकरण र त्यसमा संलग्न मानिसहरुलाई पक्राउ गरी सार्वजनिक गरेको छ । जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय भैरहवामा बुधबार पत्रकार सम्मेलन गरी प्रहरीले उक्त कार्यमा संलग्नहरु बारे जानकारी दिएको हो ।

रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको छ । असार २६ गते बुटवलमा चिनजानकै गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछानेले एक महिलालाई इसेवामार्फत् २ हजार १ सय रुपैयाँ ट्रान्सफर गर्न लगाएर दुईवटा हजारका नोट दिएकी थिइन् ।

पछि ती नोट नक्कली भएको थाहा पाएपछि पीडित महिलाले इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलमा निवेदन दिएकी थिइन् । पूर्वछानेलाई नियन्त्रणमा लिएर अनुसन्धान गर्ने क्रममा नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित प्रहरीले ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको हो ।

अनुसन्धानका क्रममा बुटवल र पोखराका आरोपीहरुका घरबाट समेत नक्कली एक हजार दरका नोट प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

डीएसपी चन्दका अनुसार पक्राउ पर्नेमा रुपन्देहीको बुटवल

उपमहानगरपालिका–११, सिर्जनानगर बस्ने बर्ष ३६ की गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछाने, कास्कीको पोखरा महानगरपालिका–१ बस्ने कृष्ण भन्ने किरण कृष्ण तिवारी, भक्तपुरको चाँगुनारायण नगरपालिका–१ बस्ने रामचन्द्र खत्री, कपिलवस्तुको बाणगंगा नगरपालालिका–२ बस्ने संजय थारु, दोलखाको सैलुङ गाउँपालिका–४ वस्ने वर्ष ३८ को पासाङ तामाङ र भारत पश्चिम बंगाल सिलुगुढी भक्तिनगर थाना बस्ने वर्ष ४९ को बासुमित्र आनन्द रहेका छन् ।

उनीहरुको घर तथा शरीर खानतलासीको क्रममा तयार भएका सक्कली जस्तो देखिने एक हजार दरका नक्कली नेपाली नोट ६ सय २२ थान बरामद गरिएको डीएसपी चन्दले बताए ।

प्रहरी फोटोकपी मेसिन, डेल कम्पनीको ल्याप्टप, नक्कली नोट कटिङ गर्न प्रयोग हुने मेसिन, नक्कली नोट प्रिन्ट गर्न प्रयोग हुने प्रिन्टर, नक्कली नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गर्ने पेपर १ कार्टुन पनि बरामद गरेको छ ।

यस्तै, नक्कली नोट बनाउन प्रयोग हुने केमिकल, लेमिलेसन मेसिन, प्लाष्टिक पेपर र ६ वटा मोबाइल पनि प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

पीडित महिलाको निवेदनका आधारमा लुम्बिनी प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय दाङ, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय र इलका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलले ‘अपरेसन चार्ली’ नाम दिएर नक्कली नोट सम्बन्धी संयुक्त अनुसन्धान सुरु गरेका थिए ।

पक्राउ गरेमा ६ जनाविरुद्ध रुपन्देही जिल्ला अदालतबाट मुद्रा सम्बन्धी कसूरमा ५ दिनको म्याद थप गरी अनुसन्धान जारी राखिएको प्रहरीे जनाएको छ । रुपन्देहीमा यसअघि पनि लुम्बिनी, सालझण्डी र बुटवलमै नक्कली नोट बरामद भएका थिए ।

articles.title: गृहमन्त्रीको आश्वासनपछि तेस्रो वार्ताको पखाईमा मिटरब्याजपीडित
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् रास्वपा बरिष्ठ नेता बालेन्द्र शाहले न्याय खोज्न कोही पनि काठमाडौं जानु नपर्ने, काठमाडौं घुम्न र पशुपतिको दर्शन गर्न मात्रै जाने अवस्था आउने भनी मधेस प्रदेशमै गएर आश्वासन दिएका थिए ।

रास्वपालाई मधेसबाट जनताले भारी मत दिएर जिताए पनि ।तर प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले भनेजस्तो न्याय नपाएपछि न्याय खोज्न मिटरब्याज पीडितको एक समूहले जनकपुरबाट काठमाडौंका लािग पैदल यात्रा अघि बढायो।

पटक पटकको सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएपछि आजित भएका उनीहरु निर्णायक आन्दोलन शुरु गरेका हुन् ।यसपाली जनकपुरबाट बाराको निजगढ आइपुग्दा गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले आश्वासनको पोको फुकाएका छन् ।

न्यायको माग गर्दै जनकपुरबाट असार २५ गते सुरु भएको मिटरब्याज पीडितको पैदलयात्रा मंगलबार छैटौं दिन बाराको निजगढ आइपुग्यो । काठमाडौंतर्फ अघि बढ्दै गरेको उनीहरुको यात्रा भने निजगढमै रोकिएको छ ।

गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ मंगलबार निजगढ पुगेर उक्त समूहसँग वार्ता गरि माग पूरा गर्ने आश्वास दिएपछि यात्रा रोकिएको हो । गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले पीडितको माग पूरा गर्न ३ दिनको समय मागेपछि उनीहरु निजगढमै रोकिएका हुन् । तर माग पूरा नभए उनीहरुको यात्रा पुनः काठमाडौंतर्फ अघि बढ्नेछ ।

पीडितहरूले तमसुक व्यवस्था खारेज गर्न, मिटरब्याजसम्बन्धी विशेष ऐन ल्याउन, मिटरब्याजका नाममा गुमेको चल–अचल सम्पत्ति फिर्ता गराउन तथा दोषीमाथि कानुनी कारबाही गर्न आफनो सरकारसँग माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

२०७९ सालदेखि निरन्तर राज्यको ढोका ढक्ढकाउँदै आएका पीडितहरुले मिटरब्याज नियन्त्रणका लागि बनेका कानुन, कार्यविधि तथा सरकारसँग भएका सम्झौताहरू प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन नभएपछि पुनः आन्दोलनको बाटो रोजेका हुन् । यसअघि उनीहरु दुई दुई पटक काठमाडौं आएर सरकारसँग सहमति गरेका थिए ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितको पैदलमार्चको श्रृङ्गखला

पहिलो पैदल मार्च

मिटरब्याज पीडित पहिलो पटक २०७९ चैत २ गते महोत्तरीको बर्दिबासबाट पैदल मार्चपास गर्दै काठमाडौं आएका थिए ।बर्दिबासबाट निस्किएका मधेशका ७२ जना मिटरब्याज पीडित ११ दिनमा काठमाडौं आईपुगेका थिए।आन्दोलन चर्की पछि चैत १८ गते सरकार र आन्दोलनकारी बिच पाँच बुँदे सहमति भयो।त्यस बेला पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड प्रधानमन्त्री थिए।सहमति अनुसार सरकारले विशेष अदालतका पूर्वअध्यक्ष गौरीबहादुर कार्कीको नेतृत्वमा जाँचबुझ आयोग गठन गर्यो।

सो आयोगमा २८ हजार भन्दा बढी उजुरी परे।पिडितको संख्या ठूलो भएपनि आयोगको म्याद सकिदाँ सम्म न्याय भने एकदम कम मात्रले पाए।जसमा १५ हजार उजुरीमाथि छानबिन भए पनि ५ हजार ५०० फस्र्यौट भएको थियो।तर अधिकांशमा भने कुनै सुनुवाई नै भएन।

दोस्रो पैदल मार्च

पहिलो पैदल मार्च भएको एक बर्ष नबित्दै मिटर ब्याज पिडित फेरि काठमाडौंमा लागि निस्किए । २०८० माघ १६ गते मेची र महाकालीबाट एकैपटक मिटरब्याज तथा ठगी बिरुद्ध पिडितहरुको पैदल मार्च निस्कियो । दोस्रो पैदल मार्चमा करिब ४ सयको संख्यामा पिडित सहभागी थिए ।

काठमाडौंमा उनीहरुको सशंक्त आन्दोलनपछि २०८० फागुन २८ गते फेरि सरकार र मिटरब्याज पिडित बिच वार्ता भइ अर्को चार बुँदे सहमति भयो ।

दोस्रो सहमतिपछि २०८० चैत ९ गते सरकारले पुनः पूर्वन्यायाधीश तेजबहादुर कार्कीको नेतृत्वमा अर्को मिटरब्याजसम्बन्धी जाँचबुझ आयोग गठन ग¥यो । तेजबहादुर नेतृत्वको आयोगमा ३२ हजार उजुरी प¥यो । तर, सबैको प्रभावकारी सुनुवाई हुन सकेन ।

आयोगको काम प्रभाकारी नभएपछि पडितले संघर्ष जारी नै राखे ।पुनः २०८१ फागुन २८ गते सरकारले पूर्व न्यायाधीश बाबुराम रेग्मीको अध्यक्षतामा अर्को तीन सदस्यीय अनुचित लेनदेनसम्बन्धी जाँचबुझ आयोग बनायो ।तेस्रो पटक गठन भएको यो आयोगमा पनि करिब १० हजार उजुरी परे । तर कार्यान्वयन भएन ।

यी आयोगहरू गठन हुनुअघि २०७९ असोज १ गते पनि सरकारले गृह मन्त्रालयका अधिकारी भीष्मराज भुषालको नेतृत्वमा मिटरब्याज अपराध नियन्त्रण सिफारिस कार्यदल गठन भएको थियो । यसपछि मिटरब्याज पीडितहरूले जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयमा उजुरी दिएका थिए । तर केहीको उजुरी सुनुवाई भएपनि अधिकांशको उजुरीको सुनुवाई नै भएन ।

तेस्रो पैदल मार्च

मिटरब्याज पीडितको तेस्रो पैदल मार्च गत असार २५ गते जनपुरको तिरहुतियागाछीबाट सुरु भएको हो । ३५ जिल्लाका चार सय भन्दा बढी पिडित सहभागी यो यात्रा १५ दिनमा काठमाडौं आइपुग्ने योजना थियो । सरकारले यसअघि सहमति गरि पटक पटक आयोग गठन गरि काम शुरु गरे पनि पूर्णता नदिएपछि उनीहरु आन्दोलित भएका हुन् । निजगढमा रोकिएको उनीहरुको यात्रा माग पूरा नभएपछि तीन दिनपछि पुनः काठमाडौं तर्फ अघि बढ्नेछ ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितको अन्त्यहीन संघर्ष

यसअघि दुइ पटक काठमाडौं सम्मको पैदलमार्च, संघीय सरकारसँग पटक पटक सहमति र तीन तीन वटा आयोग गठन। तर मिटरब्याज पीडितका समस्या ज्युका त्युँ। अनि कहिले प्रचण्ड गर्मी त कहीले झरीका बीच काठमाडौं तर्फको पैदल मार्च ।

मिटरब्याज पीडितहरु यो संघर्षको श्रृखंला माग पूरा नभएसम्म नरोक्ने योजनामा छन् । सरकारसँग पटक पटक सहमति हुने तर कार्यान्यन नहुदाँ उनीहरु पटक पटक आन्दोलनमा उत्रिन बाध्य भएका छन् । मिटरब्याज समस्या समाधानका लागि गृहमन्त्री गुरुङ समक्ष प्रस्तुत गरेका ६ बुँदे मागमाथि प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयमा छलफलको क्रममा छ ।

अब प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयको निर्णय आएपछि गृहमन्त्री र मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलनको नेतृत्वबीच पुनः तेस्रो चरणको वार्ता हुनेछ ।

articles.title: नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकमा खुशी
articles.summary:
मुगु । मुगुको सोरुगाँउपालिका ५ नेरघाटमा मोटरेबल बेली ब्रिज निर्माण सम्पन्न भएपछि यस क्षेत्रका स्थानीयवासीलाई सहज भएको छ । यस पुलले हुम्लाको करिडोरसँग सडक सञ्जाल जोड्दै वर्षौंदेखिको आवतजावतको समस्या समाधान गर्न महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेलेको छ । वर्षायाममा खोलामा पानीको बहाव बढ्दा हुने जोखिम र सास्ती पूर्ण रूपमा अन्त्य भएको भन्दै स्थानीय खुसी भएका छन् ।

मुगुको सोरुगाँउपालिका ५ नेरघाटमा बेलिब्रेज पुल निमार्ण भएपछि स्थानीय निकै खुसी भएका छन । पुर्वाधार बिकास कार्यालय मुगुले २०८१साल असार ४ गते ४ करोड ९४ लाखमा ६० मिटर लम्बाई रहेको पुल ठेक्का आह्वान गरेको थियो ।

नेरघाट बेलीब्रेज पुल २०८३ असार मसान्तमा सम्पन्न भएपछि स्थानीयलाई सहज भएको हो । नेर र ताजा गाँउका १ हजार ५ सय भन्दा बढी नागरीकले यो पुलबाट दैनिक आवजावत गर्दछन् । पहिला पुल नहुदा बाबीया (घाँस)को तुईन प्रयोग गरिन्थ्यो । त्यसपछि झोलुङ्गे पुल प्रयोगमा ल्याइयो । झोलुङ्ग पुलबाट पशुचौयाहरुलाई आवतजावत गर्न निकै समस्या हुने गरेको थियो ।

पहिला पुल नहुदा नेर र ताजा गाँउबाट अर्को गाँउ जान ४, ५ घण्टा समय लाग्थ्यो । कर्णाली करीडोर पुग्न निकै कठीन हुनुका साथै गाँउमा उत्पादन गर्ने बस्तुहरुले बजार नपाएर गाँउमै कुहीएर जाने समस्या पनि अन्त्य हुने विश्वास स्थानीयको छ । बेलीब्रीज बनेपछि समय र ढुवानी खर्च दुवै घटेको भन्दै स्थानीयको भनाई छ ।

यो पुलबाट सोरुगाँउपालिका वडा नम्बर ५ नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकहरुलाई पालिका केन्द्र ,सदरमुकाम, गमगढी ,हुम्ला जिल्लाका बिभिन्न बस्ती र कर्णाली करीडोरबाट सुर्खेत,नेपालगंन्ज जानको लागी निकै सहज भएको छ । साथै गाँउमा कृषकहरुले उत्पादन गरेका रैथाने अन्न बाली लगायत अन्य बस्तुहरुले बजार पाउनुका साथै स्थानीयको आय आर्जनमा पनि सुधार ल्याउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

मुगुको सदरमुकाम गमगढी र पालिका केन्द्रबाट निकै टाढा रहेको नेर र ताजा बस्तीका नागरीकले पुल नहुदा दैनिक भोग्नु परेको समस्या समाधानको लागी हुम्ला कर्णाली करीडोर र मुगुको नेरघाटमा पुल बनाइएको हो ।

मुगुको नेर र ताजा बस्तीका १५ सय भन्दा बढी नागरीकले दैनिक लाभ लिनुका साथै हुम्ला जिल्लाबासीलाई पनि आवतजावतमा सहज भएको छ ।

कर्णाली प्रदेश पूर्वधार बिकास कार्यालयको आर्थिक सहयोग र स्थानीय सरकारको सहजीकरणमा नेरघाट बेलिब्रेज पुल निमार्ण भएको हो ।

articles.title: ९ बुँदे सहमतिसँगै गणेश नेपाली प्रकरण समाधानतर्फ
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको त्रिपुरेश्वरमा आत्मदाह गरेका गणेश नेपालीको शव बुझ्न परिवार सहमत भएको छ । पीडित परिवारसँग आइतबार दोस्रो चरणको वार्तामा सहमति भएपछि परिवार शव बुझ्न सहमत भएको हो । नेपाली परिवार र सरकारबीच नौ बुँदे सहमति भएको छ ।

मुगुको सोरु गाउँपालिका–६ का गणेश नेपालीको आत्मदाहको घटनाको अनुसन्धान गर्न सरकारले पूर्व न्यायाधीशको नेतृत्वमा स्वतन्त्र छानबिन समिति गठन गर्ने भएको छ । सरकार र पीडित पक्षबीच आइतबार ९ बुँदे सहमति भएपछि परिवार शव बुझ्न तयार भएको छ । सहमतिअनुसार पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति उपलब्ध गराइने, शहीद घोषणा सम्बन्धी निर्णय छानबिन प्रतिवेदन, विगतको अभ्यास र प्रचलित कानुनअनुसार गरिने उल्लेख छ ।

सहमति नहुँदा पोस्टमार्टम प्रक्रिया प्रभावित भएको थियो । घटनामा संलग्न भनिएका काठमाडौं महानगर प्रहरीका नगर प्रहरी कर्मचारीलाई अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन नआउञ्जेल निलम्बन गरिने सहमति पनि भएको छ । वार्तापछि विवाद समाधानतर्फ उन्मुख भएको सरकारी पक्षले जनाएको छ ।

नेपालीका परिवारसँग भएको ९ सहमतिहरु के के ?

१.यस घटनाको सत्यतथ्य र निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न नेपाल सरकारले पूर्वन्यायाधीशको संयोजकत्वमा यथाशीघ्र स्वतन्त्र छानबिन समिति गठन गर्नेछ । उक्त समिति गठन भएको मितिले ७ दिनभित्र प्रतिवेदन नेपाल सरकारसमक्ष पेश गर्नेछ ।।

२.स्वर्गीय गणेश नेपालीलाई सहिद घोषणा गर्ने सम्बन्धमा प्रचलित कानुन, विगतको अभ्यास तथा गठन हुने छानबिन समितिको प्रतिवेदन र सिफारिसका आधारमा नेपाल सरकारले आवश्यक निर्णय प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनेछ ।।

३.घटना घटेको दिन उक्त घटनास्थलमा फिल्डमा अग्रभागमा खटिएका काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाका महानगरीय प्रहरी बलका कर्मचारीलाई पछि छानबिन आयोगको प्रतिवेदन÷सिफारिस बमोजिम जाने गरी हाललाई निलम्बन गर्न काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकालाई जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, काठमाडौँबाट लेखी पठाउने ।।

४.काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाको आगामी बस्ने कार्यपालिका बैठकको निर्णयानुसार मृतककी श्रीमतीलाई निजको योग्यता तथा क्षमताका आधारमा रोजगारी सुनिश्चित गरिनेछ । साथै, मृतककी छोरीको उच्च शिक्षासम्मको अध्ययनका लागि काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाबाट सम्पूर्ण खर्च समेतको आवश्यक प्रबन्ध मिलाइनेछ । यस कार्यका लागि नेपाल सरकारका सम्बन्धित निकायहरूले समन्वय गर्नेछन् ।

५.काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाको आगामी कार्यपालिका बैठकबाट निर्णय गराई मृतकको आश्रित परिवारलाई राहतस्वरूप यथोचित रकम उपलब्ध गराइनेछ ।

६.मृतकको अन्तिम संस्कारका लागि आवश्यक पर्ने सम्पूर्ण व्यवस्था तथा काठमाडौँमा गरिने काजक्रियाको आवश्यक व्यवस्थापन काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाबाट मिलाइनेछ ।

७.पीडित परिवार तथा आफन्तजनको तर्फबाट मृतकको शव बुझिलिने, शव परीक्षण लगायतका कानुनी प्रक्रियामा पूर्ण सहयोग र सहजीकरण गरी सद्गत गर्ने जिम्मा लिइनेछ ।

८. मृतकका एकाघरका परिवारजनको आतेजाते (यातायात) खर्च एवम् काठमाडौंमा काजक्रिया अवधिभर रहँदा–बस्दा हुने सम्पूर्ण खर्चको प्रबन्ध काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले व्यहोर्नेछ ।

९.पीडित परिवारका एकाघरका परिवारको स्वास्थ्य बीमाको कार्य स्वास्थ्य तथा खाद्य स्वच्छता मन्त्रालयबाट आवश्यक व्यवस्था मिलाइनेछ ।।

घटनाको सत्यतथ्य छानबिन समितिको निष्कर्षका आधारमा दोषी देखिएकामाथि थप कारबाही प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइने सहमति भएको छ । तर परिवारले राहत स्वरुप कति रकम पाउने भन्ने खुलाइएको छैन । पिडित परिवारको सहमतिमा उनीहरुको माग अनुसारकै रकम दिईने बताईएको छ ।

सम्झौता गर्न गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, काठमाडौं पुगेका थिए भने नेपालीको परिवारबाट श्रीमती एकमाया नेपाली, दाइ मदन नेपालीसहित हिक्मत शाही, धर्मराज शाही, मुगुका सांसद खड्गबहादुर शाही लगायत थिए । यसअघि काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले गणेशको परिवारलाई रोजगारी र निःशुल्क शिक्षाको जिम्मेवारी लिने घोषणा गरेको थियो ।

गणेशको मृत्युबारे उपत्यका प्रहरी कार्यालय, रानीपोखरीका डीआईजी गोविन्द थपलियाको नेतृत्वको पाँच सदस्यीय समितिले पनि छानबिन गरिरहेको छ । पिडित पक्षबाट १२ जना र सरकारको पक्षबाट चार जनाले सहमतिमा हस्ताक्षर गरेका छन् । पीडित पक्ष र सरकारी टोलीबीच काठमाडौं जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयमा करिब २४ घण्टा लामो वार्ता भए पछि मात्र सहमति जुटेको हो ।

articles.title: सुकुम्बासीलाई खाजामा एउटा मिठाई, होल्डिङ सेन्टर डुब्दा अलपत्र
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । १५ दिनका लागि भन्दै कीर्तिपुरको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा सारिएका सुकुम्बासी तीन महिनापछि पनि अलपत्र छन् । बाढीबाट बचाउन सारिएका भनिएका सुकुम्बासीहरु शनिबार मध्यराति बसिरहेको सेन्टरमै बाढी पसेपछि विचल्लीमा परे । सरकारको वाचा कागजमै सीमित भएको भन्दै उपेक्षा र गैरजिम्मेवारीको आरोप उनीहरुले लगाएका छन् ।

काठमाडौंका सुकुम्बासीलाई १५ दिनका लागि भन्दै कीर्तिपुरको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा सारिएको थियो । तर तीन महिना बित्दासमेत स्थायी व्यवस्थापन हुन सकेन । उल्टै शनिवार मध्यराति करिब १२ः४० बजे सेन्टरमै बाढी पसेपछि सुकुम्बासीको विजोग भएको छ ।

बालबालिका, वृद्धवृद्धा र दीर्घरोगीहरू जोखिममा परे भने सरकारको प्रतिबद्धता कागजमै सीमित भएको भन्दै पीडित आक्रोशित छन् । पीडित दलमर्दन कामीले सरकारले खाजा भन्दै एउटा मिठाइ थमाउनेबाहेक केही नगरेको आरोप लगाए । आफ्नै बसोबासको ठाउँमा फर्किन पनि नदिइएको र बाढीले रातभर सुत्न नदिँदा अब मर्नुको विकल्प नरहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

कान्छीमाया घलानले सुतिरहेको बेला पानी पस्दा छाता र मोबाइलबाहेक केही बचाउन नसकेको बताइन् । लुगाफाटा, खाद्यान्न र ओढ्ने–ओछ्याउने सबै भिजेको तथा उद्धारका लागि सुरक्षाकर्मी राति तीन बजे मात्रै आएको उनको गुनासो छ । १५ दिनका लागि भन्दै घर भत्काएर ल्याइए पनि तीन महिनासम्म अलपत्र पारिएको भन्दै उनी आक्रोशित बनिन् ।

सेल्टरमा रहेका पीडितहरुले १५ दिनको नाममा यहाँ ल्याएर बेवारिसे बनाएको भन्दै सरकारले के गर्न खोजेको भन्दै प्रश्न गरेका छन् ।

सरकारमा बस्नेहरू पनि एक दिन मर्नुपर्छ भन्ने हेक्का राख्न चेतावनी दिँदै आफूहरूमाथि अत्याचार भएको उनको गुनासो छ ।

पानी पस्ने थाहा हुँदाहुँदै यहाँ ल्याइएको आरोप पीडितहरुले लगाएका छन् । डम्बर तामाङले बाढीबाट करिब एक लाख रुपैयाँ बराबरको क्षति भएको र चप्पलसमेत नभएकाले बालबालिका नांगो खुट्टा हिँड्न बाध्य भएको बताए ।

मुटु, मिर्गौला र दमका बिरामीसमेत चिसोमा कष्टकर अवस्थामा छन् । पीडितले आश्वासन धेरै तर काम शून्य भएको भन्दै सरकारप्रति रोष पोखेका छन् । यता राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीका नेता ओजश्वीराज थापाले व्यवस्थापनमा प्राविधिक कमजोरी स्वीकार गर्दै खाना, डस्ना, ब्ल्याङ्केट र स्वास्थ्य सेवा उपलब्ध गराइरहेको दाबी गरे ।

१५ दिनको आश्वासन तीन महिनामा पनि समाधन नहुँदा सुकुम्बासी विलचित मात्रै बनेका छैनन, उनीहरुको बिचल्ली समेत भएको छ ।

होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा अनिश्चित भविष्यका साथ उनीहरु सरकारले उपेक्षा गरिरहेको महशुष गरिरहेका छन् । सुकुम्बासीसँग गरिएको वाचा र प्रतिबद्धता कार्यान्वयन नहुनुको कारण सरकारले खुलाएको छैन । सुरक्षित स्थानमा राखिएका भनिएका सुकुम्बासीहरुको कीर्तिपुरको दृश्यले उनीहरु जीवन बचाउन संघर्ष गरिरहेको देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: आगोले जल्दा ज्यान जोगाउने प्राथमिक उपचार !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आगलागी वा अन्य कारणले हुने जलनमा सही प्राथमिक उपचार अपनाउँदा गम्भीर क्षति कम गर्न सकिने स्वास्थ्य विज्ञहरूले बताएका छन् । जलेको भागमा २० मिनेट चिसो बग्ने पानी हाल्ने र तत्काल अस्पताल पु¥याउने उपाय सबैभन्दा प्रभावकारी मानिन्छ छ ।

आगलागी, ग्यास चुहावट, विद्युत् सर्ट वा तातो पदार्थका कारण हुने जलनका घटनामा समयमै सही प्राथमिक उपचार गर्न सकिए गम्भीर क्षति कम गर्न सकिने स्वास्थ्य विज्ञहरूले बताएका छन् ।

उनीहरूका अनुसार अस्पताल पु¥याउनु अघि गरिने केही सामान्य तर सही उपायले पीडितको अवस्था थप बिग्रनबाट जोगाउन मद्दत गर्छ । स्वास्थ्यकर्मीका अनुसार आगोले जलेको व्यक्तिलाई देख्नेबित्तिकै सबैभन्दा पहिले आगो निभाएर सुरक्षित स्थानमा सार्नुपर्छ । यदि लुगामा आगो लागेको छ भने पीडितलाई रोक्ने, भूईमा लड्ने, घोप्टिएर वा पल्टिँदै आगो निभाउने विधि अपनाउन लगाउन सकिन्छ वा बाक्लो कपडाले आगो छोपेर निभाउन सकिन्छ ।

त्यसपछि जलेको भागलाई तुरुन्तै चिसो बगिरहेको पानीमा करिब २० मिनेटसम्म राख्न वा पानी बगाउनुपर्छ । यसले छालाको तापक्रम घटाएर थप क्षति हुनबाट बचाउन मद्दत गर्छ । बरफ वा अत्यधिक चिसो वस्तु भने सिधै जलेको भागमा राख्नु हुँदैन यसले थप क्षति पु¥याउन सक्छ ।

यदि जलेको स्थानमा औँठी, घडी वा कसिलो गहना छ भने सुन्निनु अघि सावधानीपूर्वक हटाउनुपर्छ । त्यसपछि जलेको भागलाई सफा, सुख्खा र नटाँसिने कपडा वा स्टेराइल गजले हल्का ढाक्नु पर्छ ।

विशेषज्ञहरूले जलेको भागमा घ्यु, तेल, टुथपेस्ट, बेसार, मल्हम, माटो वा अन्य घरेलु पदार्थ नलगाउन आग्रह गरेका छन् । यस्ता वस्तुले संक्रमणको जोखिम बढाउन सक्छ र उपचारमा कठिनाइ सिर्जना गर्न सक्छ ।

जलेको फोका फुटाउन हुँदैन । यी र यस्ता प्राथमिक उपचार विधि अपनाउँदै जलनमा परेका व्यक्तिलाई तत्काल अस्पताल लैजानुपर्छ ।

आगलागी जलनमा परेका व्यक्तिलाई के गर्न हुँदैन भन्नेमा पनि हामी सचेत हुनुपर्छ । त्यसैले आगोले जलेका व्यक्तिलाई

- सिधै जलेको भागमा बरफ नराख्ने

- घ्यु, तेल, टुथपेस्ट, बेसार वा अन्य घरेलु पदार्थ नलगाउने

- फोका नफुटाउने

- जलेको छालामा टाँसिएको कपडा जबर्जस्ती नउखेल्ने

यी त भए प्राथमिक उपचार विधि । त्यसैले आगोले जलेको घटनामा नआत्तिकन धैर्यताका साथ सफा चिसो पानीको प्रयोग मात्र गर्दा पनि बिरामीले ठुलो राहत पाउँछन् । प्राथमिक उपचार लगत्तै बिरामीलाई जतिसक्दो चाँडो नजिकैको सुविधासम्पन्न अस्पताल पु¥याउनु नै सबैभन्दा बुद्धिमानी हुन्छ ।

articles.title: Substitute Torres rescues grim final to make Spain world champions
articles.summary:
Spain climbed again to the summit of world football on Sunday when substitute Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute to prise the World Cup from holders Argentina with a 1-0 victory that crowned a new era but brought precious little beauty.

The biggest prize in ‌football deserved a classic. Instead, the world’s two finest teams produced a suffocating stalemate that drifted towards penalties before Torres finally found the extra-time breakthrough with Spain’s 20th attempt on goal.

It was perhaps fitting that the final whistle sparked the game’s liveliest moments, with players pushing, shoving and falling to the ground as Argentina’s frustrations finally boiled over into a brawl.

The euphemism “one for the purists” might have been coined to describe this contest. It was a match almost entirely devoid of quality, chances and risk until Torres, introduced from the bench, finally broke the deadlock.

“It was a goal scored by 47 million people – it wasn’t even mine or from the 26 players,” the striker said. “It was destined to happen; it was meant to be a winner.”

Argentina’s talisman Lionel Messi, the second player after Brazilian great Cafu to feature in three World Cup finals, was a ⁠pale shadow of his earlier self, unable to inspire his team.

For Spain, teenager Lamine Yamal barely registered. These two had been billed as the stars of this match, but it was Spain substitutes Torres and Nico Williams who injected some much-needed energy and dynamism into a drab affair.

It was the fifth of the last six World Cup finals to go to extra time, but none of those crowds had endured such flat, joyless football.

Shot-shy Argentina

Spain, masters of the suffocating, pressing style, had nothing to press, nothing to suffocate. The Argentines were the first-ever team to fail to muster one shot — on target or off — for the entire 90 minutes of a World Cup final.

Argentina seemed content to niggle, pull shirts, shove, foul and disrupt rather than attack. In some respects, it was remarkable they finished with only one red card, Enzo Fernandez being dismissed for flattening Pau Cubarsi in stoppage time.

After more than a month of scintillating goals and exhilarating sport, this was no advertisement for what the hosts call soccer.

One can only imagine what U.S. President Donald Trump, watching alongside FIFA chief Gianni Infantino in a glassed-off VIP box, made of the spectacle. Trump later presented the World Cup trophy to the Spaniards.

In truth, this was the toughest of sells, even for the purists. Spain dominated possession but were toothless in attack.

In total, they had 20 attempts on goal, 12 on ‌target. Possession only ⁠gets you so far in a sport where goals settle results.

The official FIFA statistics registered Argentina as having two attempts at goal. None were on target and the term attempt was being used loosely.

Showbiz Razzmatazz

Singers, flags, fireworks, podiums, pop stars and Hollywood idols had flooded the pitch in the buildup to this clash. The greater surprise was that the kickoff was delayed only five minutes by all the showbiz razzmatazz.

articles.title: Roads department deploys heavy machinery as monsoon landslides disrupt highways
articles.summary:
The Department of Roads has deployed 155 pieces of heavy equipment along major highways across the country as monsoon-triggered landslides continue to disrupt traffic on key road corridors, with another 122 machines on standby to respond to emergencies.

The move comes as landslides have repeatedly blocked highways in several parts of the country, forcing road closures, traffic diversions and travel restrictions during the peak monsoon season.

Among the worst-hit routes is the Narayanghat-Muglin road, where frequent landslides at Tuin Khola have become an almost daily occurrence, repeatedly bringing traffic to a halt.

Road officials say excavators and technical teams have been stationed at vulnerable locations to clear debris immediately after landslides occur and restore traffic as quickly as possible.

With the landslide risk escalating, the Chitwan District Administration Office has also begun suspending night-time traffic along sections of the Narayanghat-Muglin road based on weather forecasts issued by the Meteorological Forecasting Division.

Following forecasts of heavy rainfall on Saturday night and Sunday, authorities imposed a complete ban on night-time movement along both the Narayanghat-Muglin and Nagdhunga-Muglin road sections.

The threat extends well beyond Chitwan.

Every monsoon, highways passing through steep hills and river corridors become highly vulnerable to landslides. This year is no exception.

Road officials have identified several high-risk routes, including the Kanti Highway, BP Highway, Nagdhunga-Muglin road, the Koshi, Karnali and Kaligandaki corridors, the Sanfe-Martadi, Bhalubang-Pyuthan and Surkhet-Nepalgunj roads, the Mechi Highway, the Galchhi-Trishuli-Syabrubesi-Rasuwagadhi road and other major arterial routes.

The under-construction Nagdhunga-Muglin road remains particularly vulnerable.

Landslide-prone locations along the highway include Furke Khola, Jhyaple Khola, 13 Kilo, Char Kilo, Ratamate, areas around Shitalbazar and Bishal Bazar, Jyamireghat, Jawang Khola, Mauwa Khola and Ghoptebhir.

The route witnessed one of Nepal's deadliest landslides in recent years when a massive slide at Jhyaple Khola in September 2024 buried parked buses and microbuses, killing 35 people.

Road officials say preventive measures have since been introduced at the site, while heavy equipment has been pre-positioned to respond immediately if fresh landslides occur.

Saujanya Nepal, chief of the Federal Highway Supervision and Monitoring Office under the Department of Roads, said the widening project itself has increased the risk of fresh landslides in some stretches.

“Because construction is ongoing, landslides are occurring not only at known vulnerable sites but also at new locations,” Nepal said.

“So far, the major landslides have been confined to a few highway sections. We have stationed machines at those locations, and once the rain stops, debris is cleared and traffic resumes.”

He said prolonged rainfall remained the biggest challenge.

“Roads have not remained blocked for long solely because of landslides. Clearance naturally takes longer if rainfall continues for an extended period. Otherwise, because excavators have been stationed strategically, traffic disruptions have generally been short,” he said.

Elsewhere, the Araniko Highway continues to face repeated disruption at Kodari, where landslides frequently block access to the Tatopani border crossing with China.

The Kanti Highway has also experienced near-daily disruptions.

Landslides regularly occur on both the Lalitpur and Makwanpur sections of the highway, a crucial route for transporting milk, vegetables and other agricultural produce to Kathmandu.

Rajan Pandey, an engineer at the Kanti Highway Road Project Office, said the highway carries more than 500 vehicles a day despite the recurring disruptions.

“On the Lalitpur side, Kalche, Takuche, Bhaise and Bhalukhola remain the most vulnerable locations,” Pandey said.

“On the Makwanpur side, landslides frequently occur at Bhattepakha, Simat and Thingan.”

He said most landslides are cleared within 15 to 20 minutes, allowing traffic to resume quickly.

“Debris falls almost every day during the monsoon, but machines are mobilised immediately,” Pandey said.

The highway suffered landslides at more than 18 locations during the September 2024 floods. Slope stabilisation and road improvement works are currently underway.

In eastern Nepal, traffic along the Rajduwali section of the Mechi Highway has remained completely blocked for a week after massive landslides.

Pawan Bhattarai, chief of the Road Division Office in Ilam, said reopening the road would take at least another week because reconstruction work is already underway.

“The contractor is working continuously, including on public holidays, but the road cannot be reopened immediately,” Bhattarai said.

Vehicles are currently being diverted through the Tilkeni-Simalgolai road, which has been repaired to serve as a temporary alternative route.

Bhattarai said persistent rainfall has also triggered landslides along the Kechana-Kanchenjunga road under the Mechi Corridor.

“Ilam has received heavy rainfall this monsoon. Frequent landslides and muddy road conditions have made maintenance particularly challenging,” he said.

To minimise prolonged road closures, the Department of Roads has strategically positioned heavy machinery along vulnerable highway sections instead of keeping equipment at regional depots.

According to the department, its Mechanical Division has deployed 155 excavators, loaders, trucks and tippers across the country, while another 122 machines remain on standby.

The division operates a total fleet of 277 heavy machines through 16 Heavy Equipment Divisions and Mechanical Offices nationwide.

Bhuwan Adhikari, deputy director general of the Department of Roads and chief of its Mechanical Division, said machinery had been positioned on every highway identified as highly susceptible to landslides.

“We have deployed excavators, loaders, tippers and trucks wherever they are needed,” Adhikari said.

“At present, the most serious problem is at Kodari on the Araniko Highway, where part of the road itself has collapsed.”

He said debris clearance could begin only after rainfall subsides and falling rocks or soil no longer threaten workers and machinery.

“It is not possible to operate heavy equipment while landslides are still active,” he said.

“Although continuous rainfall increases the risk, we have not encountered any landslide that could not eventually be cleared.”

The department has also tailored deployments according to terrain.

“In highly vulnerable locations, we have stationed two loaders and two tippers,” Adhikari said.

“In most places, one machine is sufficient. In narrow sections where debris cannot simply be pushed down the slope, we have also deployed trucks and tippers to transport the material.”

Heavy equipment has been stationed along the BP Highway at Nepalthok and Bhiman, the Khurkot-Ramechhap and Kinartar-Ramechhap sections, and several locations on the Araniko Highway and the Kaligandaki Corridor.

Machinery has also been positioned along the Balkhu-Dakshinkali road, the Naubise-Gajuri and Malekhu-Muglin stretches of the Prithvi Highway, the Chhahare-Gurjubhanjyang road and multiple landslide-prone sections of the Narayanghat-Muglin highway.

Similar deployments have been made on the Hilepani-Halesi-Diktel, Jayaramghat-Halesi, Dharan-Bhedetar, Chatara-Barahachhetra and Bhedetar-Mulghat roads, as well as along the Koshi Highway, Mechi Highway, Khandbari-Num, Phidim-Basantapur, Lahan-Kadamaha-Gaighat, Mirchaiya-Katari-Ghurmi and Saune-Gaighat-Diktel roads.

In western Nepal, machinery has been stationed along the Siddhartha Highway, the Naudanda-Nayapul-Kusma and Putalibazar-Waling roads, the Maldhunga-Baglung and Baglung-Beni sections, Dumre-Lamjung-Besisahar, Abukhaireni-Gorkha-Ghyampesal, Besisahar-Chame, Gorusinge-Sandhikharka, Tansen-Tamghas and Daunne-Butwal.

Further west, equipment has been pre-positioned along the Pili-Kalikot, Nagma-Bhulbhule-Gamgadhi, Khulalu-Salisalla, Bhalubang-Chakchake-Liwang, Hilsa-Simikot, Humla-Kalikot, Sahajpur-Phaltude, Sanfebagar-Achham, Chheda-Matela-Jajarkot and Jajarkot-Dolpa roads, as well as the Bhasu Bhir section of the Bhimdatta Highway and vulnerable stretches of the Rapti, Mid-Hill, Koshi and Madan Bhandari highways.

articles.title: Foreign study costs outpace growth in Nepal’s service exports
articles.summary:
Every year, thousands of Nepali students leave the country for higher education, taking billions of rupees in foreign exchange out of Nepal. Their educational expenses have become the single largest driver of Nepal’s widening service trade deficit, overshadowing gains from tourism and the country’s fast-growing information technology (IT) exports, according to the government’s latest trade report.

Nepal recorded a service trade surplus of Rs9.85 billion in the fiscal year 2015-16, exporting services worth Rs136.47 billion while importing Rs128.62 billion. Less than a decade later, the situation has reversed dramatically.

By the fiscal year 2024-25, service exports had risen to Rs238.66 billion, but service imports had surged to Rs329.60 billion, leaving Nepal with a service trade deficit of Rs90.94 billion.

Education services accounted for the largest share of service imports.

Nepal spent Rs138.48 billion on education services in 2024-25 alone. Spending has grown at an average annual rate of around 18 percent over the past three fiscal years.

By contrast, education service exports stood at just Rs3.89 billion during the same period and have grown by only about 2 percent annually over the past three years.

As more Nepali students enrol in universities abroad, spending on tuition, accommodation and living expenses has climbed to record levels, making education the country’s largest service import.

While education is widening the deficit, the IT sector is emerging as one of Nepal’s most promising service export industries.

Software development, business process outsourcing, digital freelancing, web and mobile application development, graphic design and other IT-enabled services are generating rising foreign earnings, although much of the income remains absent from official statistics.

Telecommunications, computer and information services generated exports worth Rs22.33 billion in the fiscal year 2024-25, accounting for 9.36 percent of total service exports.

Industry experts, however, say the real figure is far higher.

A study by the Institute for Integrated Development Studies estimated Nepal’s IT service exports at Rs67.93 billion ($515 million) in 2022. Industry representatives argue that exports have increased further since then, but much of the income is never recorded because freelancers and software companies often receive payments through overseas platforms, foreign bank accounts or third-country companies instead of Nepal’s formal banking system.

Gaurav Raj Pandey, president of the Nepal Association for Software and IT Services (NAS-IT), said most foreign currency earned by IT professionals is recorded as remittance rather than service exports.

“As a result, there are no reliable statistics on Nepal’s IT service exports,” he said.

According to Pandey, NAS-IT estimates industry growth by tracking annual salary increases among IT professionals.

“The IT sector has been growing by 15 to 20 percent annually, and salaries are increasing at roughly the same pace,” he said.

The government report also acknowledges that official statistics underestimate the true size of Nepal’s IT exports because many freelancers receive payments outside Nepal’s banking system.

It says the rapid expansion of Nepal’s digital workforce and growing global demand for outsourced technology services offer one of the country’s best opportunities to narrow the widening service trade deficit.

Capturing IT earnings through formal channels could substantially strengthen Nepal’s foreign exchange reserves and reduce dependence on traditional service exports such as tourism, the report says.

Software development, web and mobile applications, graphic design, digital marketing, business process outsourcing, data processing and freelancing are becoming increasingly competitive in international markets. As more young Nepalis acquire digital skills and demand for remote services continues to grow worldwide, IT is emerging as a major source of export earnings.

With reforms to foreign exchange regulations, easier international payment systems and tax incentives, IT-based services could become Nepal’s largest service export industry, according to the report.

The service sector now contributes more than 62 percent of Nepal’s GDP. In fiscal year 2024-25, services accounted for 21.44 percent of the country’s total foreign trade.

The report says Nepal’s impending exit from the Least Developed Country category will gradually reduce preferential market access, export concessions and development assistance.

“In this context, rather than relying solely on limited and traditional merchandise exports, developing high-value-added, knowledge-based and competitive service exports must become a key pillar of Nepal’s national economic strategy,” it says.

The report identifies tourism, electricity, construction and IT as the country’s major growth sectors for future service exports. It notes that Nepal’s new international airports in Bhairahawa and Pokhara, expanding hydropower exports to India and Bangladesh, and the growing international competitiveness of Nepali construction firms could all help diversify service exports.

The expansion of energy trade is expected to make a significant contribution to service exports, foreign exchange earnings, and Nepal’s participation in the regional energy market.

Construction services are also emerging as a potential export industry. Over the past two decades, rapid infrastructure development has significantly enhanced the experience and capacity of Nepali construction companies, engineers, technicians, and skilled workers.

Although institutional capacity still needs strengthening to undertake large and complex projects, several Nepali construction firms have already won international tenders and completed projects abroad.

Given the competitive skills and labour costs of Nepali professionals, there is considerable potential to expand construction service exports to South Asia, the Middle East, and beyond.

The report also shows that Nepal maintained a service trade surplus between fiscal years 2015-16 and 2017-18 before slipping into persistent deficits.

Travel remained Nepal’s largest service export category in 2024-25. It earned Rs88.66 billion and accounted for 37.15 percent of total service exports. Other business services contributed Rs57.56 billion, followed by government goods and services at Rs34.28 billion, transportation at Rs27.89 billion and IT services at Rs22.33 billion.

On the import side, travel services—which include education, tourism and overseas medical treatment—totalled Rs223.72 billion, accounting for 67.87 percent of total service imports.

Transportation services followed at Rs61.41 billion, while insurance and pension services, other business services and telecommunications, computer and information services made up the remaining major import categories.

The report says Nepal’s service exports are becoming increasingly diversified. While tourism once dominated the sector, exports are now expanding in information technology, digital services, professional consulting, construction, education, healthcare and electricity, laying the foundation for a more resilient and sustainable service export sector.

articles.title: Elephant safaris at crossroads as Chitwan weighs ethical tourism shift
articles.summary:
On Friday afternoon, nature guide Samjhana Tiwari posted a video on Facebook showing a long queue of tourist vehicles heading towards the Baghmara Buffer Zone Community Forest for elephant and boat safaris.

“There are so many vehicles. You would not even see this many at a bus station,” Tiwari said in the video.

The footage came during the off-season, yet it showed a steady stream of visitors arriving for jungle activities in the forest area adjoining Sauraha, Nepal’s largest wildlife tourism hub. Tiwari had posted the video to draw attention to growing concerns over crowd management after seeing vehicles carrying tourists move directly towards elephant and boat boarding points.

But a Supreme Court order published just a day earlier had shifted the conversation in Sauraha from managing tourist crowds to questioning the future of one of Chitwan’s most recognisable attractions.

The court’s directive asking authorities to explore alternatives to elephant safaris has opened a debate among tourism entrepreneurs, conservationists, elephant owners, and local communities over whether traditional elephant rides can continue and how a transition to more ethical models could affect the local economy.

On September 14, 2021, animal rights advocates, including Sanjay Adhikari of the Forum for Protection of Public Interest (Pro Public), filed a writ petition at the Supreme Court seeking stronger legal protection for elephants. The petition called for an end to practices considered cruel to elephants, proper documentation of elephant ownership transfers, action against illegal trade, restrictions on prolonged chaining and a shift away from using elephants for rides, arguing that they should be used primarily for viewing.

The Supreme Court issued its verdict on December 17, 2025. The full text of the order, passed by a joint bench of Justices Hari Prasad Phuyal and Tek Prasad Dhungana, was published on the court’s website last Thursday.

The 62-point order includes several directives on elephant welfare, with one of its key provisions calling for alternatives to elephant safaris. The decision has since triggered a wider debate in Chitwan’s tourism sector about how to balance animal welfare with the economic importance of an activity that has supported local businesses for decades.

Point 48 of the order states that allowing tourists to ride elephants must be reconsidered from an animal welfare perspective and that alternative approaches should be adopted. At the same time, the court acknowledged the economic role of elephant safaris in generating income, promoting tourism and creating employment in places such as Sauraha.

For decades, elephant safaris have been among the main attractions for visitors to Chitwan National Park and its surrounding areas. Tourists, especially international visitors, have traditionally taken elephant rides to explore grasslands and forests to spot rhinos, deer, wild boars and other wildlife.

Tourism entrepreneurs say any transition away from elephant rides must be carefully planned, as thousands of people depend directly or indirectly on wildlife tourism.

“We cannot ignore animal welfare, but we also have to consider the livelihoods of people who depend on elephant safaris,” said a tourism entrepreneur in Sauraha. “The transition should be practical and involve all stakeholders.”

Conservationists, however, see the court order as an opportunity to redesign Chitwan’s wildlife tourism model.

They argue that alternatives such as jeep safaris, guided jungle walks, canoe trips and birdwatching tours can offer visitors rewarding wildlife experiences without relying on elephant rides.

“Tourism must evolve with changing global practices,” said a conservationist involved in wildlife protection. “The focus should be on observing animals in their natural habitat rather than using them as a means of transport.”

Elephant owners and mahouts, meanwhile, have raised concerns about what will happen to domesticated elephants if safari rides are discontinued. Many elephants currently used in tourism are maintained through income generated from safari operations.

Stakeholders say the government must prepare a transition plan covering elephant care, employment support and the development of alternative tourism products before introducing major changes.

The debate comes as Nepal’s wildlife tourism sector faces the challenge of balancing conservation priorities with economic realities. Chitwan National Park attracts hundreds of thousands of domestic and international visitors every year, and tourism remains a key source of income for communities surrounding the park.

Sauraha, located on the edge of Chitwan National Park, has long built its tourism economy around jungle activities, including elephant safaris. Local businesses fear that a sudden end to elephant rides without viable alternatives could affect hotels, guides, transport operators and communities dependent on tourist spending.

Environmental groups, however, argue that Nepal must gradually move away from tourism models that rely on animals for entertainment and align with growing international demand for ethical wildlife experiences.

As authorities and stakeholders begin discussions on implementing the court’s directive, the challenge for Chitwan will be finding a way to protect elephants while preserving the economic lifeline that wildlife tourism provides to local communities.

Point 48 of the court order states that “forcing a gradually disappearing species like the elephant to carry humans appears to be inherently irresponsible behaviour”. The court observed that an elephant’s spine, legs and body structure were not naturally designed to carry human weight. Carrying heavy loads for long periods and walking continuously, it said, can cause physical stress, including joint and leg problems.

“Thus, using elephants merely as tools for entertainment or tourism is incompatible with our obligation towards their value and welfare as living beings,” the order states.

In Point 51, the court suggested replacing traditional elephant safaris with alternatives such as “elephant walks” and “elephant bushwalks”.

“In accordance with welfare standards, it is essential to establish legal and policy frameworks to replace elephant safaris and cruel tethering systems in Nepal, transitioning towards an ethical and eco-friendly model,” the order states.

The court has also encouraged Nepal to adopt wildlife tourism practices used in other countries, including elephant-friendly walks and observing elephants from a safe distance without direct interaction.

But implementing such changes could have major economic consequences for communities around Chitwan National Park, where elephant safaris have long been a source of income.

The Baghmara Buffer Zone Community Forest, located on the outskirts of Sauraha, covers only 215 hectares. Yet at its peak, the forest generated around Rs30 million annually, according to former chairman Jitu Lama Tamang. Nearly one-third of that revenue came from elephant safaris.

Around seven or eight community forests surrounding Chitwan National Park rely heavily on elephant safaris for income. Elephant rides have not been allowed inside the national park for nearly 15 years. The activity is now limited to buffer zone community forests bordering the park.

Government-owned elephants are not used for tourist rides. The safaris are operated using privately owned domesticated elephants.

“Chinese tourists have a strong interest in elephant safaris. Even during the monsoon, when tourist arrivals usually decline, Chinese visitors have continued to arrive, and almost all of them take elephant rides. After safari income declined following Covid-19, Chinese tourists brought some hope,” said Bhuwaneshwar Prasad (BP) Chaudhary, chairman of Baghmara Buffer Zone Community Forest.

He warned that replacing elephant safaris without proper alternatives could significantly reduce the forest’s income.

However, Chaudhary also acknowledged that demand for elephant rides has been declining. In December 2014, Munich-based organisation Pro Wildlife had urged tourism operators to reduce activities involving elephant rides, arguing that such practices were inconsistent with modern wildlife tourism standards.

“European tourists generally do not ride elephants anymore. Nepali tourists may try it once but rarely repeat the experience. These days, Chinese tourists are the main group taking elephant rides,” Chaudhary said.

Former Baghmara chairman Tamang said local communities have also become increasingly concerned about keeping domesticated elephants near settlements. He said captive elephants often attract wild male elephants, increasing the risk of human-wildlife conflict.

“There were discussions about keeping domesticated elephants together on the edge of the forest rather than scattered around settlements. The government needed to provide land for that purpose. The Supreme Court order has also moved towards a sanctuary model,” Tamang said.

He said the time had come to ensure that tourism activities do not come at the cost of elephant welfare.

Most elephant safaris in Chitwan operate around Sauraha. The elephants involved are affiliated with the United Elephant Operation Cooperative Limited.

According to cooperative chairman Dipendra Khatiwada, the cooperative currently has 30 elephants, while another 14 operate independently. Around 38 to 40 elephants are used for safaris daily.

The cooperative was also named as a defendant in the writ petition filed at the Supreme Court.

Khatiwada said elephant safari operations had already declined significantly. Before the Covid-19 pandemic, the cooperative alone had around 63 elephants working in safaris. As tourism collapsed during the pandemic, some rented elephants were returned while others were sold to India.

“Everyone now agrees that the elephants that remain must be managed properly,” he said.

However, he said developing alternatives would require government support and clear policies.

“We have been asked to find alternatives to safaris, but this cannot be done through our efforts alone. How far will an ‘elephant walk’ extend? How will it operate? What policy framework supports it? The government must answer these questions,” Khatiwada said.

He said tourism stakeholders would respect the court order but cautioned against an abrupt transition.

“Replacing elephant safaris overnight could disrupt the entire tourism sector. We need enough time, clear policies and promotional campaigns to introduce new models properly,” he said.

Khatiwada also urged the government to address broader issues related to elephant management.

“The court has shown concern for the welfare of the elephants we rear. But it would have been better if it had also addressed issues such as the shortage of grazing land and difficulties in providing enough grass for elephants,” he said.

Tourism entrepreneur Hari Bhakta Ghimire said the government must introduce a clear policy following the court ruling.

Ghimire, who opened a hotel in Sauraha in 1982, introduced elephants for safari operations soon afterwards. He currently owns two adult elephants and a two-year-old calf.

He argued that elephant safaris have been closely linked with Chitwan’s tourism history and should not be viewed only from the perspective of animal welfare concerns.

“People in Nepal and India have used elephants for riding since ancient times. Elephant safaris in Chitwan began with the establishment of the national park. Tiger Tops, which opened in 1964, eight years before the park was established, also operated elephant safaris. It is a long-standing tradition,” Ghimire said.

He said tourism entrepreneurs had invested heavily in caring for domesticated elephants and that these realities should also have been considered.

Basu Dhungana, a conservationist and owner of a tourist resort in Kumroj near Sauraha, said the shift away from elephant rides is becoming inevitable as global tourism increasingly moves towards ethical wildlife experiences.

Dhungana, who opened his resort three years ago, does not offer elephant safaris. He said the government, community forests, hotels and tourism entrepreneurs should work together to develop genuinely elephant-friendly tourism models.

Bed Kumar Dhakal, spokesperson for the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, said elephant management was a serious issue for the department.

He said the government would work to implement the court’s directives while balancing them with the practical concerns of elephant owners.

Chitwan National Park remains Nepal’s most popular wildlife destination, attracting around 300,000 domestic and international visitors annually. Besides elephant safaris, the park offers jeep safaris, boat trips on rivers and streams bordering the park, and guided jungle walks.

The challenge now is to determine whether Chitwan can preserve its appeal as a wildlife destination while moving towards a tourism model that protects elephants and sustains the communities that have long depended on them.

articles.title: Who will save libraries?
articles.summary:
Once, libraries were hubs of learning and engaging places for individuals to exchange ideas. Despite the politically challenging times of the Panchayat era, libraries flourished, and so did the habit of visiting them. But decades of official neglect and declining public investment have pushed many libraries to the brink of extinction. The closure of the Kathmandu Valley Public Library at Bhrikutimandap is a telling example. The Social Welfare Council, which manages the library, shut it down in April, citing unpaid rent of around Rs30 million. While the unpaid dues have been presented as the immediate cause, the closure ultimately reflects the government’s failure to recognise and protect libraries as essential public institutions. Instead of finding ways to further promote a library that housed around 60,000 books, journals, reports and booklets, served some 3,000 members and attracted around 200 daily visitors, authorities chose to shut it down.

Policymakers often speak of taking education to new heights, but the ambition rings hollow when a public library serving those who cannot afford expensive books, academic journals or reliable internet services is forced to shut down. Despite the rise of mobile phones, the internet and digital resources, the importance of libraries has not reduced. We just need to look at well-managed libraries such as the Nepal National Library, the Kaiser Library, and the Tribhuvan University Central Library to understand the importance of libraries even today. A large number of people throng these reading spaces as not everyone has the privilege of having a library-like environment at home or in the rooms they rent. Often, it is easy to access reference materials and books from libraries and read in their quiet corners.

Nepal should therefore rethink the role of public libraries. In the past, during the Rana regime, people fought for intellectual freedom, demanding knowledge that would be accessible to all. That history deserves to be remembered. Today, people have more access to knowledge, but many libraries continue to operate as they did decades ago, failing to adapt to the changes in how people learn. So, they should be equipped with both traditional collections and digital catalogues, e-books, academic databases, multimedia resources and high-speed internet services.

The responsibility of managing libraries should extend beyond the federal government. Many community libraries in the country were established by passionate founders and activists or through community initiatives. Now, they reportedly struggle to survive due to a lack of resources. Municipalities and communities should therefore recognise libraries as essential public spaces and invest in them. The private sector can also collaborate by investing in technology and library resources. The country desperately needs a vision for public libraries that meets the demands of modern learning practices while preserving their fundamental value.

Several countries around the world continue to expand public libraries as community learning centres, digital resource hubs and cultural spaces. They subsidise libraries to make them accessible to all, acknowledging that their purpose is to generate knowledge. Their practice is worth emulating. However, Nepal, with the recent closure of a library due to unpaid rent, is moving in the opposite direction. The current government boasts a Cabinet and Parliament filled with ‘intellectual’ and ‘educated’ individuals. Such a government has a greater responsibility to protect institutions of learning. If they cannot save libraries, it is difficult to imagine who will.

articles.title: Together for climate-resilient agriculture
articles.summary:
Sometimes the unintended consequences of certain decisions prove more significant than their intended goals, as is happening with the merger of federal ministries. In a bid to reduce the state’s financial burden and improve administrative efficiency, the Government of Nepal has undertaken a significant administrative restructuring by merging several ministries. This includes the integration of the Ministry of Agriculture Development (MoAD) and the Ministry of Forests and Environment (MoFE) into the new Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment (MoAFE).

The late Minister Shailaja Acharya first proposed merging agricultural and forestry institutions in the early 1990s. The rationale then was rooted in a practical reality: At the farmers’ level, the boundary between agriculture and forests often blurs, making integrated management of farms and forests essential for sustainable development. Despite this recognition, institutional and administrative rigidities prevented the merger for decades. That proposal has finally been realised at a time when climate change has become a serious threat to our agriculture.

While fiscal savings and broader administrative efficiency primarily drove the current restructuring, the creation of the MoAFE also stands as a welcome development from a climate change perspective. It establishes a strong institutional foundation for an integrated approach increasingly recognised globally—placing the agro-food system at the centre of both climate action and sustainable development. Building on the former MoFE’s strong legacy in climate leadership, the new ministry now has a valuable opportunity to drive this agenda forward.

Climate connection

The erstwhile MoFE served as the primary nodal ministry for climate change, leading the development of key national climate policies and frameworks, coordinating with other ministries and facilitating the integration of climate change considerations into sectoral plans at both the federal and subnational levels. Notably, it coordinated the formulation of Nepal’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP), which outlines priority adaptation programmes across climate-vulnerable sectors, including agriculture. The formation of the new MoAFE now places these coordination responsibilities under a single ministry that directly oversees agriculture, creating a stronger platform for mainstreaming climate responses within the agro-food system.

Agriculture and food security feature prominently in the NAP, with flagship programmes focused on enhancing agricultural productivity through climate-resilient water management systems. This is particularly critical in Nepal, where droughts have chronically affected farming for decades. Drying local water sources, depleting soil moisture and shrinking aquifers have severely affected farming. Recurrent droughts, especially during the planting season and sometimes mid-crop cycle, combined with floods, soil erosion and landslides, have left farmers struggling to cope with increasingly unreliable weather patterns.

The collapse of winter rainfall across much of the country is no longer a temporary anomaly but a sign of a fundamental and possibly irreversible shift in climate patterns. The consequences for the food system are already stark: Farmers are being pushed towards bankruptcy, local food shortages are emerging and the national food import bill is rising sharply.

In this context, merging agriculture and forestry into the new MoAFE becomes even more compelling. By placing both sectors under unified political and administrative leadership, the new ministry is better positioned to understand their interlinked vulnerabilities, eliminate coordination barriers and promote genuinely integrated management of farms and forests. However, like any newly formed institution, the MoAFE will need to overcome several operational and institutional challenges to fully realise its potential.

The challenges

One of the most immediate challenges facing the new MoAFE is the development of a shared mission and vision—a task complicated by the fact that professionals from the two erstwhile ministries come from distinctly different disciplines, each with its own approaches, priorities and a tendency to assert the primacy of its own sector. An added layer of complexity is the management of water resources, a critical element for both agriculture and forestry, yet one that neither ministry has historically managed with sufficient depth beyond basic utilisation.

While it has long been claimed that maintaining good forest cover helps conserve water sources, this assertion has rarely been subjected to rigorous scrutiny. Institutions responsible for forest protection were not required to demonstrate measurable improvements in water availability or spring recharge. As a result, despite having more than 46 percent of its land under forest cover, Nepal continues to lose mountain springs. Hence, the challenge for the new institution will be to gently unlearn and relearn with a deeper and more nuanced understanding of the forest-water relationship.

Climate change has too often been narrowly framed as a problem of floods and landslides. This limited perspective helps explain why, despite numerous policy declarations, the country still lacks effective agricultural programmes for farmers to adopt at scale to counter growing climate threats. There is growing recognition that many long-relied-upon solutions, such as rainwater harvesting, are inadequate to address the scale and nature of the emerging challenges. So far, the steps taken have not made food and water systems truly resilient.

Even robust evidence of climate impacts on agriculture, generated by the government’s own scientifically rigorous studies, such as the National Climate Change Survey (NCCS), often fails to translate into decisive action. The NAP rightly stresses mainstreaming climate change into sectoral plans and budgets to ensure more transparent, efficient and cost-effective actions. Yet, while effective mainstreaming would improve risk tracking, accountability and impact assessment, it remains a formidable challenge that the new ministry must overcome.

Renewed hope

Recent weeks have provided sobering reminders of what lies ahead. Europe experienced record-shattering heatwaves, while China and India suffered catastrophic flooding, deadly landslides and widespread urban inundation. Given rising global temperatures, similar extremes are increasingly likely in Nepal. The critical question is whether, at the current pace of efforts and level of understanding, the country can realistically tackle these threats and safeguard its agriculture and food security.

With limited resources and fragile ecosystems, Nepalis are exceptionally vulnerable to environmental shocks that have historically forced us to adapt to the adversities. A prime example is the traditional practice in narrow mountain valleys of reclaiming flood-damaged farmland by strategically diverting silt-laden floodwater onto affected fields. For generations, communities have used this method to sustain food security despite operating in highly constrained and risk-prone landscapes with very limited arable land. These traditional techniques helped make scarce farmlands and, by extension, local food security, more resilient to floods.

While such traditional measures are no longer sufficient on their own to counter emerging threats, they offer a valuable foundation upon which more effective, climate-resilient solutions can be built. We still need to develop more effective ways to protect our food and water systems from the growing vagaries of nature. In this context, the merger of the agriculture and forestry ministries, though primarily driven by fiscal calculus and administrative goals, has renewed hope that a more integrated and effective approach to building climate-resilient agriculture may finally emerge.

articles.title: Challenges of living with history
articles.summary:
Historical interpretation of current events has become the most touted subject in recent times. There is a contradiction here. Some time separates us from the events of history. But there is no point in time when a particular event or set of events is relegated to history. This problem arises in a society where events occur frequently. In common parlance, people say we are living in the most so-and-so moments of history. I have heard some people call yesterday’s event history. There is no denying that presentism is the creator of history. Everything starts from the present. But there are certain metaphors in Nepali history that recur more often than any others in discussions and interpretations. This is the subject of another essay. Here, I would like to begin with our practice of defining history in terms of the dominant characters of the events.

Nepal is unique in matters of recording events—some small and others quite big—in terms of their effect. If we take some time to browse through our history, we can see that events have occurred in Nepali society at a fast pace. Each event has ushered in changes. The major events of the 104-year autocratic rule of the Rana oligarchy were homogeneous in character. They were events of the autocracy that involved succession and the seizing of opportunities to hold power, but after its downfall in 1951, or after the establishment of democracy in Nepal, a different kind of power struggle and succession order became the norm, shaping the changes.

It would be tautological to repeat the order of events in modern history. We are all familiar with the major historical events of the modern era, such as the fall of the Rana regime; the coalition government of the Rana and Nepali Congress; the panchayat rule, a dictatorial order established by the Shah king Mahendra in 1960; the Maoist war of 1996-2006; the end of monarchy in 2008, making Nepal a federal democratic republic; elections and the formation of party governments; and the big Gen Z-led demonstrations that pushed the established party government out of power, bringing former Chief Justice Sushila Karki into office as Nepal’s first female prime minister, who conducted the March election that brought today’s parliament and the government of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. How each change introduces norms of action is a subject of interest and concern.

We have accepted that our actions are governed by the norms of democratic change. They should be so if we want to consolidate the democratic system. Certain ethics and philosophies should guide our actions. We are talking about the important moments of change. Talking about the norm and spirit of liberal democracy, Fareed Zakaria, writer, says in Age of Revolutions, “We uphold freedom of speech, rather than favouring specific speech. We want elections to be free and fair, rather than favouring one candidate. We make law by consensus and compromise, not by degree. But increasingly there are those—frustrated by the process, sure of their virtue, loathing the other side—who want to ban what they regard as ‘bad’ speech, make policy by fiat, or even manipulate the democratic process.”

If we are nurturing such norms, we should abandon them. I want to link this statement to the cursory view of Nepali history that I just presented. The ethic is that the individual speaks for the voice of the times. For example, individual acts of courage can spark revolutions. The Associated Press, in an obituary on 17 December 2011, wrote: The self-immolation of a vegetable-seller in Tunis named Mohamed Bouazizi triggered a revolution. That sparked a wave of rebellions across the Arab world in 2011. But I am not trying to draw an analogy between this story and that of Ganesh Nepali here.

Some commotion occurs when a young person decides to end their life in a public place in broad daylight. That creates sensation and triggers discussion among people about the method chosen to end their lives. This could be a woman or a man, young or old. Here, we are talking about a 25-year-old ride-sharing driver named Ganesh Nepali, who poured petrol and set himself on fire. He died later in the hospital. The motorcycle he had bought on a huge loan was his minuscule universe, embodying his presentism and futurity. But the process involved in its purchase and the modality of its use very clearly made it a symbol and metaphor of the political and economic system of Nepal.

The debate triggered after his death, both in the legislature and in the media across different orders, foregrounded the political, economic, administrative and moral issues of current Nepali society. The public and parliament have been debating this topic with great rigour. A report says an agreement has been reached between Nepali’s family and the government. This incident has slowly gone down in history as a narrative of temporal significance. I appreciate the government’s prompt response in this matter. What follows the incident should be viewed from a realistic perspective.

But Ganesh Nepali’s self-immolation has highlighted important moments in the current mood and mode of Nepali society. The Nepali history we alluded to at the opening of this essay saw many moments when the youth felt they should sacrifice their lives. Many have already done so. History speaks. But what should alarm us at this stage of Nepali history is a sense of frustration among Nepali youth and adults that could propel them to take such actions. There are many people, experts and scholars who can analyse the state of mind of youth and the nature of their frustration. Though it may be an arduous task to trace every form of youth frustration, it would be important to identify its sources. Sociologists, writers, politicians, psychologists and spiritual gurus may have their own ways of addressing these issues.

But at the end of the day, those who rule the country should use their energy, judgement and policies to address the root causes of the frustration and ennui gripping the public’s mind. It is realistic to expect a particular government to solve the problems, but those in opposition parties, the media and the intelligentsia also have responsibilities in such matters. I watched the parliamentary debate the other day and felt encouraged by the free opinions expressed by both the ruling party and the opposition. That is the right step towards history-making.

articles.title: Is Rs25,000 enough compensation for a state-induced humanitarian crisis?
articles.summary:
The government of Nepal’s decision to provide Rs25,000 as compensation to families displaced by recent settlement clearances raises a difficult but necessary question: Can a one-time payment adequately compensate for the destruction of not only homes but also the social, economic and emotional foundations that sustain people’s lives?

Forced displacement isn’t simply the loss of shelter. It disrupts a full spectrum of life and wellbeing, including access to health care, education, nutrition, livelihoods, sexual and reproductive health rights, social networks and support systems, privacy, safety and human dignity.
