काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलन प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गत वर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गते देशमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोह र त्यसक्रममा भएका गम्भीर मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटनासम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ पुगेको छ ।

नेपालभित्र प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न चौतर्फी माग भइरहेका बेला आयोगले करिब १० हजार पृष्ठ लामो उक्त प्रतिवेदन जेनेभास्थित मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा पेश गरेको छ।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली र गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखकसहित उच्च अधिकारीहरूमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धानको सिफारिस गरिएको यो प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पुगेसँगै अब सरकारमाथि कूटनीतिक र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढ्ने देखिएको छ ।

गएको भदौ २३–२४ गतेको जेनजी विद्रोहसम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय मानव अधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय ओएचसीएचआर जेनेभामा पेश भएको छ ।

यो प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अब सरकारलाई थप दबाब पर्नेछ । जुन १५ देखि जुलाइ ७ सम्म जेनेभामा चलेको ह्युमन राइट काउन्सिलको २४औँ बैठक र ६२ औँ सत्रमा राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगका सदस्य मिहिर ठाकुरले नेपालमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोहको मानवअधिकार अवस्थाका विस्तृत विवरणसहितको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि सरकारलाई बुझाएको जानकारी दिँदै सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वय गर्नैपर्ने जानकारी गराएका थिए ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगले पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनलाई नोटमा राखेको छ । सरकारलाई मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अरु दबाब पर्नेछ । जेनेभा बैठकमा भाग लिन आयोगका सदस्य ठाकुरसँगै आयोगकी उपसचिव माया शर्मा पनि पुगेकी थिइन ।

सरकारमाथि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढाउने रणनीति

आयोगभित्रैका केही अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगर्ने आशंका बढेपछि आयोगले प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पठाएको हो ।

नेपालमै प्रतिवेदन पूर्णरूपमा सार्वजनिक गर्न आग्रह मानव अधिकार आयोगले आग्रह गरे पनि त्यो सम्भव नभएको बताउने गरेकाले पनि अब जेनेभाबाटै थप प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढ्न सक्ने अवस्था बनेको छ ।

प्रतिवेदनमा को–कोमाथि अनुसन्धान सिफारिस ?

जेनजी आन्दोलनमा भएको दमन, गोली प्रहार, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी तथा विध्वंसका घटनाबारे आयेगको प्रतिवेदन करिब १० हजार पृष्ठको छ । तर आयोगले प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश मात्रै सार्वजनिक गरेको थियो ।

उक्त प्रतिवेदनमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली, तत्कालीन गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखक, तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङ, तत्कालीन प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक चन्द्रकुवेर खापुङ लगायतमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएको छ ।

यसैगरी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको विध्वंसमा कलाकार, पत्रकार, इन्फ्लुएन्सर तथा हाल संसद् र सरकारमा रहेका केही व्यक्तिहरूमाथि पनि थप अनुसन्धान गर्न आयोगले सिफारिस गरेको छ ।

आन्दोलनका घटनाबारे आयोगको निष्कर्ष

पूर्ण प्रतिवेदनमा भदौ २३ देखि २६ सम्मका घटना समेटिएका छन् । कसले कोसँग संवाद ग¥यो ?के–के कुरा भयो ? सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगो लगाउनेसम्ममा कसको योजना थियो भन्ने समेटिएका छन् ।

भीड कसरी उग्र बन्यो, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी गर्ने योजना कसरी बनेको थियो भन्ने विवरण पनि प्रतिवेदनमा समावेश छ । आयोगले अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक केही प्रमाण, विशेषगरी गोलीका अवशेष बुलेट संकलन गर्न नसकिएको स्वीकार गरेको छ ।

ओली–लेखकले नै मागेका छन्, प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि

आयोगको पूर्ण प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न माग भइरहँदा फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएका पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् एमाले अध्यक्ष ओली, पूर्व गृहमन्त्री एवम् कांग्रेस नेता रमेश लेखक, पूर्व सञ्चार मन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङले प्रतिवेदनमाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै आयोगसमक्ष निवेदन दर्ता गराएका छन् ।

प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश झिकिएको र केही अंश थपिएको आशंकापछि उनीहरुले प्रतिवेदन माग गरेका हुन् । ओलीको तर्फबाट छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन माग गर्दै एमाले नेता महेश बर्तौलाले असार १२ गते आयोगमा निवेदन दर्ता गराएका थिए ।

ओलीले आयोगको बैठकको निर्णय नम्बर १७७ को प्रमाणित प्रतिलिपि, लिली थापा नेतृत्वको समितिले आयोगमा पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि, प्रतिवेदनमा थपघट गरिएको अंश र थपघट गर्नुको कारणसमेत माग गरेका छन् ।

यस्तै, रास्वपा सभापति रवि लामिछानेलाई कारागारबाट बाहिर निकाल्न गएको आरोप लागेका सांसद दीपक बोहोराले पनि आयोगमा निवेदन दिएका थिए । आयोगले भनेको समयमा आफू अस्पतालमा रहेको उनको दलिल छ ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा प्रतिवेदन पेश भएपछि के हुन्छ ?

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले अब चार चरणमा प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउँछ ।

पहिलो चरण : अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखः–

प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको आधिकारिक अभिलेखमा दर्ता हुन्छ । यसले नेपालमा मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन भएको दाबी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय निगरानीमा प्रवेश गर्छ ।

दोस्रो चरण : प्रश्न र स्पष्टीकरणः–

मानव अधिकार परिषद्का सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूले नेपाल सरकारसँग स्पष्टीकरण माग्न सक्छन् ।

तेस्रो चरण : सिफारिसः–

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय वा विशेष प्रतिवेदकहरूले नेपाललाई अनुसन्धान, पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति वा जिम्मेवार व्यक्तिमाथि कारबाही गर्न सिफारिस गर्न सक्छन् ।

चौथो चरण : निगरानीः–

नेपालले ती सिफारिस कार्यान्वयन ग¥यो कि गरेन भनेर आगामी सत्रहरूमा पुनःसमीक्षा हुन्छ ।

जेनजी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा दबाब

जेनजी आन्दोलनको प्रतिवेदन अब नेपालको आन्तरिक राजनीतिक विवाद मात्र रहेन, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार बहसको विषय बनेको छ । मानव अधिकार परिषद्को ६२औँ सत्रमा यसबारे औपचारिक जानकारी प्रस्तुत भइसकेकाले नेपाल सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेमा आगामी सत्रहरूमा थप प्रश्न उठ्न सक्छन् ।

यद्यपी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेकै कारण कुनै देशलाई तुरुन्त प्रतिबन्ध भने लाग्दैन ।तर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आलोचना बढ्छ । मानव अधिकार सम्बन्धी वार्षिक प्रतिवेदनमा नकारात्मक उल्लेख हुन्छ । यसको असरले वैदेशिक सहायता र विकास साझेदारहरूको दबाब बढ्न सक्छ ।

त्यस्तै, विशेष प्रतिवेदक वा अनुसन्धान टोली पठाउने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। नेपालमा विगतमा द्वन्द्वकालीन मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका विषयमा संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले पटक–पटक चासो व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

यस्ता घटनामा कुन कुन देशलाई प्रतिबन्ध लागेको छ ?

मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका आधारमा विभिन्न देशहरूमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको उदाहरणहरु छन् । म्यानमारमा सैन्य दमन र मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनको घटनामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ भने इरानमा प्रदर्शनकारीमाथि दमन गरेको भन्दै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघन भएको निश्कर्षमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ।

त्यस्तै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटना छानबिन गरेर कारवाही नगरेका कारण बेलारुस, गृहयुद्ध र मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका कारण सिरिया लगायतका देश प्रतिबन्धमा परेका छन् ।

articles.title: Panel finds no basis to prosecute security chiefs over September killings, home minister refuses report, PM yet to receive it
articles.summary:
A government committee reviewing recommendations to prosecute senior security officials over the September 8-9 Gen Z protest violence, which left scores dead, most of them by police, has concluded there is insufficient evidence to pursue criminal charges.

Nearly two weeks after completing its work, however, the report remains undisclosed as Home Minister Sudan Gurung reportedly declined to receive it and Prime Minister Balendra Shah has yet to grant the committee a time for its submission.

The panel, headed by former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, completed its work before its term expired on July 6. However, the report has still not been formally handed over to the government. The delay has raised questions about the administration’s willingness to act on one of the most politically sensitive recommendations arising from last year's deadly protests.

According to officials familiar with the process, members of the committee visited the Ministry of Home Affairs on July 9, intending to submit the report. During a meeting attended by the ministry’s secretary Raj Kumar Shrestha and other senior officials, Home Minister Gurung declined to receive the document, asking the committee to submit it directly to the prime minister instead.

“The minister said he would first consult the prime minister and then arrange a suitable time for the report to be handed over,” a home ministry official told Kantipur. “No appointment has been fixed since then.”

The committee’s tenure has already expired and has not been extended.

Rama Acharya, information officer at the ministry, said she was unaware of the status of the report.

“I have no information regarding the report. You may need to inquire with the prime minister’s office or the committee itself,” she said.

According to committee members, the panel has prepared a report of more than 75 pages after reviewing evidence, consulting former and serving officials, and examining the findings of the Gauri Bahadur Karki-led commission of inquiry.

The report concludes that while there were serious shortcomings in planning, command and crowd management, the available evidence does not support criminal prosecution of the security personnel deployed during the protests.

A committee member said the home ministry’s political leadership has already been briefed on the report’s conclusions.

“The prime minister may not have had time to receive the report because of his busy schedule,” the member said.

The committee was formed after the Gauri Bahadur Karki commission recommended criminal proceedings against senior officials who commanded security operations during the September protests. A total of 76 people were killed as a result of the violence, with many succumbing to injuries in the days that followed.

The commission concluded that the top security leadership had failed to intervene even though clashes between protesters and security forces continued for around four hours before a curfew was imposed.

It recommended criminal action against Chandra Kuber Khapung, then chief of Nepali Police, on two counts, including culpable homicide through criminal negligence and recklessness.

It also recommended prosecuting former home secretary Gokarna Mani Duwadi, then chief of Armed Police Force Raju Aryal, former National Investigation Department chief Hutraj Thapa and former Kathmandu chief district officer Chhabilal Rijal under Section 182 of the National Penal Code for culpable homicide resulting from reckless conduct.

Following the March 5 general elections, the first Cabinet meeting of the Rastriya Swatantra Party-led government under Prime Minister Balendra Shah decided to implement the commission’s recommendations. However, instead of immediately acting against the security officials, the Cabinet formed a separate expert committee to examine whether criminal prosecution was warranted.

Implementation of the commission’s recommendations was subsequently delayed after the arrests of KP Sharma Oli, who served as prime minister during the protests, Ramesh Lekhak, who was home minister at the time, and several others.

The Prem Raj Karki committee has now reached a markedly different conclusion.

According to committee members, investigators were unable to determine which officers fired live rounds during the protests or identify the specific firearms used.

The report notes that no ballistic examination was conducted on the bullets recovered after the incident. It also points out that the protest site was washed on September 9, making subsequent forensic examination difficult.

The committee says statements given by lower-ranking personnel deployed during the operation also failed to establish who fired the fatal shots.

“Considering the available evidence and the circumstances, we concluded that criminal liability cannot be established,” a committee source said.

The committee, however, has recommended departmental action against security officials, arguing that significant operational failures occurred before and during the protests.

According to sources familiar with the report, it identifies weaknesses in police command, planning and coordination, and recommends disciplinary action under the Police Act rather than prosecution under criminal law.

The report also proposes clearer guidelines on the use of force and recommends strengthening human rights and crowd-control training for security personnel.

It concludes that security agencies failed to anticipate that the protests could escalate into widespread violence and criticised inadequate logistical preparation, including the absence of sufficient barricades and water cannons.

“There were clear shortcomings in command and coordination at the operational level,” a committee member said. “Departmental action is necessary to ensure such failures are not repeated.”

The report also analyses the sequence of events that led to multiple protester deaths.

Before finalising its findings, the committee consulted a wide range of current and former officials, including then-Kathmandu Valley Police Office chief and incumbent Inspector General of Police Dan Bahadur Karki, former police chief Khapung, former chief secretary Ek Narayan Aryal, representatives of the Former Nepal Police Organisation Forum and the Former Armed Police Force Association, as well as officials from the home and law ministries.

Committee members said they held detailed discussions on crowd psychology, the deployment of security forces, available crowd-control equipment and the preparedness of personnel stationed in Kathmandu during the protests.

“We were not authorised to record fresh statements, but we reviewed previous testimonies and held discussions with several individuals involved,” one member said. “Those findings have been incorporated into the report.”

Most security officials consulted during the review argued that prosecuting officers for actions taken while performing official duties would set a dangerous precedent.

“They maintained that if there had been professional lapses, those should be addressed through departmental proceedings under the Police Act or the Civil Service Act rather than criminal prosecution,” a committee source said.

The committee also examined how other countries dealt with security personnel involved in the use of force during protests and incorporated comparative international practices into its analysis.

As part of its review, members watched CCTV footage recorded during the demonstrations and examined other documentary evidence.

“The narrative that the protests were suppressed emerged very early,” a committee source said. “The report analyses how that perception developed and the circumstances surrounding it.”

Besides former judge Prem Raj Karki, the committee included former Nepal Police additional inspector general Tek Prasad Rai and former Armed Police Force assistant inspector general Subodh Adhikari.

With the report yet to reach the prime minister’s desk, its recommendations, and the government’s next move on one of the most contentious chapters of last year’s protests, remain uncertain.

articles.title: Judiciary left reeling from Gen Z protest impact as case clearance almost halved
articles.summary:
The Gen Z protests that swept across the country on September 8 and 9 last year have severely hit the country’s judicial system. With courts operating under significant limitations, the national case clearance rate plummeted to just 55 percent in the fiscal year 2025-2026.

According to the Supreme Court, out of the 357,023 pending cases lodged with various tiers across the country, only 196,474 were settled, leaving a backlog of 160,549 cases. This marks a sharp decline from the previous year’s overall clearance rate of 65.69 percent.

The Supreme Court recorded the lowest performance, settling only 29.46 percent of its cases in 2025-26, compared to 42 percent in 2024-25. High courts wrapped up 70.36 percent of their caseload against 74.61 percent previously, while district courts resolved 55.61 percent, down from 66.25 percent. Other tribunals managed to settle 41.67 percent, a major drop from last year's 56.34 percent.

Various reports show that the nationwide Gen Z protests caused an estimated total economic loss of Rs84.5 billion, with the judiciary bearing a heavy blow. Protesters destroyed or burnt approximately 936,000 legal case files and documents, crippling ongoing litigations.

The structural damage to the judiciary alone was estimated at Rs2.8 billion. A total of 23 court premises were struck, including the Supreme Court, the Special Court, seven high courts, and 14 district courts. Among them, 10 buildings were completely destroyed, nine suffered partial damage, and four sustained minor issues.

The Supreme Court sustained the heaviest blow, with its main historical building heavily ruined, resulting in losses worth Rs1.23 billion. Across the nation, infrastructure damage stood at Rs1.65 billion, vehicle losses amounted to Rs615.1 million, and office equipment damage totalled Rs538.5 million.

Supreme Court spokesperson Arjun Koirala stated that judicial activities remained virtually suspended for nearly four months after the movement. "The destruction of vital files and court property brought hearings to a standstill," said Koirala. "Severe damage to our central servers disrupted systems nationwide, preventing the judiciary from achieving its yearly targets."

Even courts that escaped direct vandalism suffered from the technological breakdown. Lal Bahadur Kunwar, acting Chief Judge of the Patan High Court, explained that the technical fallout halted their work for two months. "Although our buildings were not physically attacked, the loss of central databases and files from other courts left us unable to conduct full hearings," said Kunwar.

Special Court Chairman Sudarshan Dev Bhatta also linked the performance drop to the structural challenges. "The combination of the September riots, infrastructure loss, and scheduled judge transfers hindered our efficiency," said Bhatta. "It took substantial time to restore essential IT equipment and servers destroyed in the fire."

Bhatta added that thanks to collaborative recovery efforts, the Special Court was restored within four months, allowing them to initiate a targeted campaign to clear backlogs. The Special Court eventually settled 155 out of 261 cases, achieving a 59.38 percent resolution rate, with 106 cases remaining.

Top-performing judges by case disposal

Despite the operational challenges, several judges managed to achieve high performance numbers. In the High Court category, Judge Tek Narayan Kunwar recorded the highest number of settlements. Known for introducing digital initiatives and modern e-courts during his previous tenure at the Special Court in Kathmandu, Kunwar maintained his quick pace after his transfer to the Janakpur High Court.

Other top-performing High Court judges included Tikaram Acharya, Jagat Bahadur Thapa, Somkant Mainali, Narishwar Bhandari, Jagadish Ghimire, Gokarna Dangi, Krishna Prasad Subedi, Rajuram Silwal, and Kailash Prasad Subedi.

At the district level, Judge Rajendra Singh Bhandari of the Kanchanpur District Court led the list for the highest number of verdicts. He was followed by Madhav Prasad Ghimire, Hari Prasad Sharma Upadhyay, Kapil Mani Gautam, Bishnu Prasad Gautam, Roshan Gajurel, Manoj KC, Durga Bahadur Bhusal, Manoj Kumar Srivastava, and Bhuwan Singh Thapa.

articles.title: उच्च अदालत पाटनमा ११ हजार ४६८ मुद्दा फर्छ्यौट
articles.summary:
उच्च अदालत पाटनले गत आर्थिक वर्ष (२०८२/०८३) मा ११ हजार ४६८ मुद्दा फर्छ्यौट गरेको छ।

अदालतमा कूल लगत १६ हजार १३९ मुद्दा रहेकामा ११ हजार ४६८ मुद्दा फर्छ्यौट भएको हो।

न्यायालयले दुई वर्ष नाघेका र १८ महिना नाघेका मुद्दा शून्यमा झार्न सफल भएको छ। त्यस्तै, एक वर्ष नाघेका ३५३ रहेका छन्।

मुख्य न्यायाधीश लालबहादुर कुँवरले न्यायपालिकाको पाँचौँ पञ्चवर्षीय रणनीतिक योजनाअनुसार १८ वर्षमुनिका मुद्दा शून्यमा झार्न सफल भएको जिकिर गरे।

‘विकास निर्माण र राजस्व असुलीका मुद्दालाई विशेष प्राथमिकता दिएका छौँ,’ उनले भने।

उच्च अदालत पाटनले चालु आर्थिक वर्षमा ७४० थान मुद्दा फर्छ्यौट गरेको र एक वर्ष नाघेका थुनुवा मुद्दा १२ थान बाँकी रहेको जनाएको छ।

मातहतका जिल्लामा सिन्धुपाल्चोकले ७७.४, रसुवाले ७५.६ र जिल्ला अदालत काठमाडौंले सबैभन्दा कम ४२.३ प्रतिशत मुद्दा फर्छ्यौट गरेका छन्।

articles.title: Cervical cancer screening in Kathmandu finds 90 women positive for HPV
articles.summary:
Ninety women who underwent random cervical cancer screening carried out by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City have tested positive for human papillomavirus (HPV).

According to officials at the municipal health department, the women had no symptoms and were unaware of their condition until the screening.

“Of the total positive cases, 12 were infected with HPV-16 and 13 with HPV-18,” said Chandra Bhatta, focal person of the cervical cancer screening programme of the metropolis. “The remaining 65 women were infected with other types of HPV.”

Human papillomavirus is a viral infection that spreads through skin-to-skin contact and is a leading cause of cervical cancer—the second-most common cancer in the developing world. Cervical cancer is a major cause of death among Nepali women, with hundreds diagnosed every year.

Although the exact number of patients suffering from cervical cancer in Nepal is not known, it is estimated that at least four women die of cervical cancer every day.

The screening was carried out between March 30 and May 4, during which 2,975 women were examined. Of them, 2,779 underwent HPV DNA testing and 1,450 underwent genotype testing of the HPV virus. DNA testing detects HPV genetic material in cells collected from the cervix, while genotyping identifies the specific type of HPV present in the cervical cell samples.

As the city office had a limited number of testing kits, only 1,329 women were tested specifically for HPV types 16 and 18. HPV types 16 and 18 are estimated to cause about 70 percent of cervical cancer cases.

“First, we organise a screening camp for around a month and then perform other testing, including biopsy, mammogram, ultrasound scanning and others, which takes several weeks,” said Bhatta. “Our findings show that many women, who believe they are healthy may be living with various forms of cancer and infected with cancer-causing viruses.”

Officials say the finding also shows that women in Nepal are infected not only with HPV types 16 and 18, but also with dozens other HPV types. HPV types 16 and 18 are frequently associated with invasive cervical cancer compared to other types, meaning that they are more carcinogenic than other types.

Experts say HPV has more than 200 types, ranging from low-risk to high-risk strains. Around 40 infect the genital tract, and around 14 types are classified as high-risk because they can cause cervical and other cancers. Low-risk types generally cause genital warts or no symptoms at all.

Health officials said colposcopy was performed on all 90 women who tested positive for HPV. It is a medical procedure in which a doctor closely examines the cervix, vagina and vulva using a colposcope—a special instrument with a bright light and magnifying lenses.

Six women underwent polypectomy to remove uterine polyps, and 24 underwent cervical biopsy.

Eleven of the women who tested positive for HPV were diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (4 high-grade and 7 low-grade), which refers to precancerous changes in cells lining the cervix.

Doctors say cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is not cancer, but if left untreated, high-grade lesions can develop into cervical cancer over time.

Nepal has included the HPV vaccine in its routine immunisation programme and provides a single dose to all 10-year-old girls. The HPV vaccine, included in the routine immunisation list, targets types 16 and 18 of the virus.

Apart from screening for cervical cancer, the health department of the city office had also carried out breast examinations on 2,961 women, and mammography was performed on 411 of them. Breast biopsy was performed on four women, and of them, two tested positive and are currently receiving treatment.

“Most cancer patients in Nepal seek treatment only after symptoms start to emerge,” said Dr Ujjwal Chalise, executive director at the Bhaktapur Cancer Hospital. “Symptoms often do not appear in the initial stages of the disease, and by the time they do, it is often too late, resulting in poor treatment outcomes.”

Experts say local governments should ensure that services for basic cancer screening are available in local health facilities, stressing that early detection markedly improves treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Real estate revenue hits three-year high as buyers rush before tax hike
articles.summary:
Nepal collected Rs60.74 billion in revenue from real estate transactions in the fiscal year 2025-26, the highest amount recorded in three years, as buyers and sellers rushed to complete deals before a tax increase and renewed restrictions on land subdivision came into effect.

According to the Department of Land Management and Archives, revenue from real estate transactions reached the figure in the fiscal year that ended in mid-July. The collection was significantly higher than the Rs42.42 billion recorded in 2023-24 and the Rs41.16 billion collected in 2022-23.

Monthly data show that revenue peaked in mid-June to mid-July at Rs11.95 billion, the highest monthly collection of the fiscal year. The lowest monthly collection was recorded in mid-October to mid-November, when the government collected Rs2.75 billion.

Revenues hovered between Rs2.75 billion and Rs3.28 billion through the autumn, before seeing a slight bump to over Rs5 billion in the winter months. The revenue collection trend then improved towards the end of the fiscal year, hovering between Rs5.24 billion and Rs6.26 billion during the spring before surging to Rs11.95 billion in the final month.

The sharp rise in the final month was accompanied by a jump in real estate activity.

The department recorded 70,480 new property purchase and sale deeds in mid-June to mid-July, compared with 54,724 in the previous month and 58,886 in mid-April to mid-May. Overall, 193,028 real estate-related transactions were recorded during the month.

Real estate businesses said the increase was driven mainly by concerns over higher capital gains tax and renewed restrictions on land subdivision from the start of the new fiscal year.

The government, through the budget for 2026-27, increased the capital gains tax on real estate sales. The tax on profits from the sale of properties held for five years or more has been raised to 7.5 percent from 5 percent, while profits from properties held for less than five years now face a 10 percent tax, up from 7.5 percent.

The new tax rates came into effect from July 17.

Bhesh Raj Lohani, former president of the Nepal Land and Housing Developers’ Federation, said many people accelerated transactions before the tax increase and the return of land subdivision restrictions.

“Transactions increased significantly in the final month because people wanted to avoid the higher capital gains tax and complete deals before land subdivision restrictions were restored,” Lohani said.

Nepal has also been struggling to complete land classification required under the Land Use Regulations.

As of the last week of June, only 340 of the country’s 753 local governments had completed land classification in categories including agricultural, residential and industrial areas. The remaining 413 local governments had not completed the process.

Land subdivision has been halted in these local governments.

The government had earlier amended the Land Use Regulations 2022 for the third time, temporarily allowing land subdivision in municipalities that had not completed land classification. However, local governments that failed to complete the classification process within the extended deadline have again faced restrictions since July 17.

Under the current system, land subdivision can only take place after local governments complete land classification. Despite repeated extensions and regulatory changes, many municipalities have yet to complete the process.

Lohani said the possibility of renewed restrictions also pushed people to complete transactions before the deadline.

“Since land subdivision has again been stopped in municipalities without classification, many people rushed to complete real estate transactions,” he said.

He added that lower bank interest rates had also contributed to a gradual recovery in the real estate market, as investors began moving money from bank deposits into land and housing.

“Interest rates have declined. People have started investing instead of keeping money in banks,” Lohani said. “However, real estate transactions are likely to decline in July and August, which are traditionally the off-season.”

Along with transactions, land subdivision activity also increased sharply in the final month of the fiscal year.

The department recorded 212,779 land subdivision cases in mid-June to mid-July, compared with 143,857 in the previous month. New land subdivision cases increased from 62,457 in the previous month to 93,906 during the same period.

After restrictions were restored, subdivision cases fell to 42,563 in the first month of the new fiscal year.

Meanwhile, the department issued a notice on Monday mandating that all real estate transactions over Rs30 million in metropolitan and sub-metropolitan cities be conducted exclusively through licensed real estate companies.

articles.title: The record Nepal noticed not
articles.summary:
There is a half-second when a hamstring tears at full sprint, in which the body keeps believing it is still running. Aayush Kunwar was through the bend of the 200 metres at the 2024 National Games—into the straight where the race stops being about speed and becomes about holding your shape while your legs come apart—when the muscle in the back of his right thigh gave way. He pulled up and limped off the track; the race gone, the season with it.

I should explain why that matters now. This July, on a track in Los Angeles, Kunwar ran the 200 metres in 21.87 seconds. The Nepali national record, 21.92 seconds, had stood since 1995–the year he was born. It had outlasted three decades of sprinters who came and went without touching it. Nor did he merely reach it; he ran through it, just the way he has done everything in this sport: Alone, on his own money, with no federation standing behind him. I know this because for years, I lived in the room next to his.

We have been roommates twice, two decades apart. Once as schoolboys in Kathmandu and again in San Francisco, both of us in our twenties, still working out what our lives were going to be. Living beside him taught me what the sport actually asks of a person. I watched him come home from a full day as a financial analyst and go straight to the floor to do the physiotherapy he had taught himself. I filmed him on the university tracks around the city, hoping for sponsors to notice. But the camera caught the smallest part of it. Most of his hours had no audience, and nothing about them looked like much: A man on a borrowed track, running the same repetitions until the light gave out.

What I never worked out, in all those years close to it, was ‘why’. Not why anyone runs, but why he ran like this, at this cost, for a sport that gave back so little and so slowly. He could not tell me, and I don't think he knew himself. What stayed with me was that he ran anyway.

A sport is supposed to give an athlete five things: Coaching, physiotherapy, competition, travel and the money that makes the other four possible. Aayush built each of them himself, from parts. He coached his own recovery over the phone. He turned his body into a long experiment in nutrition, worked out between spreadsheets at his day job. He gathered his competition from other Nepali runners scattered across other countries' tracks. When there was no sponsor, he filmed the work and asked strangers to help fund a plane ticket for it. He is not only a sprinter. He is a one-man federation, a fundraiser, an organiser, a recruiter and an athlete who has spent his best years trying to move an entire country's sport a few inches forward.

So when Nepal could not get its National Games off the ground this year, he did not treat it as someone else's failure to mourn. He organised a race himself. He flew home with running shoes packed around his clothes and gave them to athletes who had none. The sport had not done much for him; he had decided, somewhere along the line, to do something for the sport instead.

There is a plain lesson in his 21.87-second record, and we should not let the celebration bury it. A record does not survive for 30 years because it is superhuman. It survives that long because year after year, nobody is given what they need to chase it. Aayush's whole career is the proof of it, and his run this July is the rebuttal he wrote himself. Imagine what a runner like him does with an actual system behind him. Then imagine how many runners like him we have already lost for the want of one.

He is not done though. There are Asian Games ahead, and World Championships, and he means to be there. But the records were never really the point. For a decade, he has been quiet proof of a single idea that one person, with enough discipline and without permission from anyone, can pick up a country's sport and carry it somewhere new. The record he set this summer will fall one day, and there is a fair chance the man who breaks it will again be the same man who just set it. Until then, he will keep doing what he has always done alone, after the workday, on whatever ground will have him, faster than the country that forgot to build him a track.

articles.title: स्पेनमा विश्वकप उत्सव मनाउने क्रममा एक जनाको मृत्यु
articles.summary:
स्पेनले विश्वकप जितेपछि उत्सव मनाउने क्रममा एक १३ वर्षीय बालकको मृत्यु भएको छ।

पोर्चुगलको सिमाना नजिकै रहेको सलामान्का प्रान्तको मध्ययुगीन शहर सिउडाड रोड्रिगोमा सोमबार उत्सव मनाउने क्रममा पानीको फोहोरा भत्किँदा १३ वर्षीय बालकको मृत्यु भएको छ भने अर्का एक बालक घाइते भएका छन्।

शहरको केन्द्रमा रहेको अर्बोल गोर्डो फाउन्टेनमा सयौं बासिन्दाहरू उत्सव मनाउन भेला भएका थिए।

articles.title: भारतमा ‘कक्रोच’ आन्दोलन चर्कियो, संसद्‍मा हजारौँ युवाको मार्च प्रयास
articles.summary:
भारतको राजधानी नयाँ दिल्लीमा युवाको नेतृत्वमा चलेको ‘कक्रोच जनता पार्टी’ (सीजेपी) आन्दोलनका हजारौँ समर्थकले सोमबार संसद् भवनतर्फ मार्च गर्ने प्रयास गरेका छन्।

प्रदर्शनकारीहरूले शिक्षा क्षेत्रमा देखिएका अनियमितता, परीक्षा प्रश्नपत्र चुहावट र सरकारी जवाफदेहिताको माग गर्दै आन्दोलन गरेका हुन्।

प्रदर्शनकारीहरू दिल्लीको जन्तर–मन्तरबाट संसद् क्षेत्रतर्फ अघि बढ्न खोजेका थिए। तर प्रहरीले अनुमति नदिएको भन्दै सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा बनाएको थियो।

केही स्थानमा प्रदर्शनकारी र सुरक्षाकर्मीबीच तनावसमेत भएको र प्रहरीले भीड नियन्त्रणका लागि लाठी तथा अश्रुग्यास प्रयोग गरेको समाचारहरूमा उल्लेख छ।

‘कक्रोच आन्दोलन’ सुरुमा सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत व्यंग्यात्मक अभियानका रूपमा सुरु भएको थियो।

बेरोजगार युवालाई ‘कक्रोच’सँग तुलना गरिएको एउटा विवादास्पद टिप्पणीपछि यो अभियानले गति लिएको बताइएको छ। पछि यो शिक्षा प्रणाली सुधार, परीक्षा व्यवस्थापन र सरकारी उत्तरदायित्वको मागसहित ठूलो युवा आन्दोलनमा परिणत भएको हो।

आन्दोलनकारीहरूले भारतका शिक्षामन्त्री धर्मेन्द्र प्रधानको राजीनामासहित परीक्षा प्रणाली सुधारको माग गरेका छन्। उनीहरूले मेडिकल तथा अन्य प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक परीक्षामा देखिएका प्रश्नपत्र चुहावट र व्यवस्थापकीय कमजोरीप्रति सरकारको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएका छन्।

प्रदर्शनमा विद्यार्थी, युवा, अभिभावक तथा विभिन्न क्षेत्रका मानिसहरूको सहभागिता रहेको बताइएको छ। आन्दोलनका प्रतिनिधिहरूले सरकारसँग संवादको माग गर्दै आफ्ना माग सम्बोधन नभएसम्म दबाब अभियान जारी राख्ने बताएका छन्।

‘कक्रोच जनता पार्टी’ नाम भए पनि यो परम्परागत राजनीतिक दल नभई युवाहरूले सुरु गरेको आन्दोलनकारी समूहका रूपमा परिचित भएको छ।

पछिल्लो प्रदर्शनले भारतमा युवा असन्तुष्टि र शिक्षा सुधारको विषयलाई फेरि राष्ट्रिय बहसमा ल्याएको छ।

articles.title: कक्रोज जनता पार्टीका नेता संसद भवन प्रवेश गरेपछि बाहिरिए प्रधानमन्त्री मोदी
articles.summary:
भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीमा कक्रोज जनता पार्टी (सिजेपी) को ‘चलो संसद’ मार्च संसद भवननजिक पुगेपछि सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारिएको छ।

सोमबार जन्तर–मन्तरबाट सुरु भएको मार्च संसद भवनतर्फ अघि बढेपछि सुरक्षा निकायले संसद् परिसर वरिपरि निगरानी र सुरक्षा व्यवस्था थप कडा बनाएका हुन्।

प्रदर्शनकारीहरूले संसद भवननजिकको ब्यारिकेड तोड्ने प्रयास गरेपछि प्रहरीले अश्रुग्यास प्रहार गर्नुका साथै लाठीचार्ज गरेको भारतीय सञ्चारमाध्यम इन्डिया टुडे ले जनाएको छ।

घटनाका बेला संसद्को मनसुन अधिवेशन जारी थियो। बाहिर प्रदर्शन चर्किरहेका बेला संसद्को बैठक केही समयपछि स्थगित गरिएको जनाइएको छ।

यसैबीच, प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदी संसद भवनबाट बाहिरिसकेका छन्।

प्रदर्शनको नेतृत्व गरिरहेका कक्रोज जनता पार्टी (सिजेपी) का संस्थापक अभिजित दिप्केलाई प्रहरीले नियन्त्रणमा लिएको बताइएको छ।

articles.title: ‘रोल न.१’ को व्यापार करोड नाघ्यो, ‘भागदौड’ले कति कमायो ?
articles.summary:
चलचित्र विकास बोर्ड बक्स अफिस आइतबारसम्म विवरण सावर्जनिक भएको छ। नेपाली तीन चलचित्र सिनेमाघरमा प्रदर्शनरत भए पनि विवरण भने दुईको सार्वजनिक भएको छ।

चलचित्र निर्देशक जोन योञ्जन निर्देशित चलचित्र ‘रोल न।१’ ले आफ्नो शनिबार ५१ औँ दिन सफलतापूर्वक पूरा गरेको छ।चलचित्र विकास बोर्डका आधिकारिक बक्स अफिस विवरण अनुसार चलचित्रले गत आइतबारसम्म १ करोड ७८ लाखको व्यापार गरेको भने ७१ हजार ३ सय ६९ वटा टिकेट बिक्री भएको छ।

गौंथलीको बक्स अफिस विवरण भने अर्को सोमबार सार्वजनिक हुने छ।

articles.title: संसदमा प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग प्रश्नोत्तर कहिले ?
articles.summary:
प्रतिनिधिसभा नियमावली, २०८३ कार्यान्वयनमा आएसँगै मन्त्रीहरूले संसद्मा नियमित प्रश्नोत्तरमा सहभागी हुन थाले पनि प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले भने हालसम्म संसद्मा औपचारिक प्रश्नोत्तर सामना गरेका छैनन्।

प्रतिनिधिसभा नियमावलीको व्यवस्था अनुसार प्रधानमन्त्री वा प्रधानमन्त्रीको कार्यक्षेत्रसँग प्रत्यक्ष सम्बन्धित महत्वपूर्ण विषयमा सभामुखले प्रत्येक महिनाको पहिलो हप्ताको कुनै एक दिनको बैठकको पहिलो एक घण्टा प्रश्नोत्तरका लागि निर्धारण गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था छ। यही व्यवस्थाअनुसार प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग सांसदहरूले प्रत्यक्ष प्रश्न गर्न पाउनेछन्।

असार ३१ गते बसेको प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठक साउन १४ गतेसम्मका लागि स्थगित भएकाले अब बस्ने बैठकमा प्रश्नोत्तर कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन हुने सम्भावना छ। नयाँ नियमावली असार १८ गते प्रतिनिधिसभाबाट पारित भएको थियो।

यसअघि असार १७ गते प्रधानमन्त्री शाह आकस्मिक रूपमा संसद् बैठकमा उपस्थित भएर सांसदहरूले उठाएका प्रश्नको जवाफ दिएका थिए। भारतसँग सम्बन्धित अभिव्यक्तिलाई लिएर विपक्षी दलहरूले आलोचना गरेपछि प्रधानमन्त्रीले त्यसबारे स्पष्ट पारेका थिए। तर त्यो औपचारिक प्रश्नोत्तर कार्यक्रम भने थिएन।

प्रधानमन्त्री नियुक्त भएयता साढे तीन महिनाको अवधिमा शाह सात पटक प्रतिनिधिसभा बैठकमा उपस्थित भएका छन्। संसद् सचिवालयका अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार विगतका प्रधानमन्त्रीहरू पनि नियमित रूपमा संसद्मा उपस्थित हुने अभ्यासमा सधैं देखिएका थिएनन्।

संसदीय व्यवस्थामा प्रधानमन्त्रीको संसद् उपस्थित र जवाफदेहिता महत्वपूर्ण विषय मानिन्छ। बेलायतमा प्रधानमन्त्रीले प्रत्येक साता सांसदका प्रश्नको सामना गर्ने अभ्यास रहेको छ भने भारतमा पनि संसद्को प्रश्नोत्तर समयमा प्रधानमन्त्रीको सहभागिता रहने गर्छ।

नेपालमा पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई संसद्प्रति थप उत्तरदायी बनाउने उद्देश्यले प्रश्नोत्तर प्रणाली राखिएको हो। अब प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले कहिलेदेखि यो व्यवस्थालाई नियमित रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्छन् भन्ने विषयमा चासो बढेको छ।

articles.title: सडक बालबालिका मुक्त नेपाल बनाउने अभियानमा सरकार: दैनिक उद्धार र गस्ती जारी
articles.summary:
महिला, बालबालिका, लैङ्गिक तथा यौनिक अल्पसङ्ख्यक र सामाजिक सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गत सञ्चालित बालबालिका खोजतलास समन्वय केन्द्र (१०४) मार्फत सडक बालबालिका मुक्त नेपाल बनाउने राष्ट्रिय लक्ष्यअनुरूप जोखिमपूर्ण अवस्थामा रहेका सडक बालबालिकाको खोजतलास, दैनिक गस्ती तथा उद्धार कार्य तीव्र गतिमा सञ्चालन भइरहेको छ।

मन्त्री सिता बादी पदबहालीपश्चात् मन्त्रालयले सडक बालबालिकाको संरक्षणलाई उच्च प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै दैनिक गस्ती, उद्धार तथा पुनर्स्थापनासम्बन्धी कार्यलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाएको छ।

यसक्रममा सडकमा जोखिमपूर्ण अवस्थामा रहेका, भीक्षा माग्न बाध्य भएका तथा जीविकोपार्जनका लागि पानी, मास्कलगायतका सामग्री बिक्री गर्न बाध्य बालबालिकाको नियमित पहिचान गरी उद्धार गर्ने, अस्थायी संरक्षण प्रदान गर्ने, मनोसामाजिक परामर्श उपलब्ध गराउने, अभिभावकलाई आवश्यक सचेतना प्रदान गर्ने तथा आवश्यकतानुसार पुनर्स्थापनाको प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउने कार्य निरन्तर सञ्चालनमा रहेको छ।

मन्त्री बादीले प्रत्येक बालबालिकालाई सडकको जोखिमपूर्ण जीवनबाट मुक्त गरी सुरक्षित वातावरण, शिक्षा, संरक्षण र सम्मानपूर्ण भविष्य सुनिश्चित गर्नु सरकारको प्राथमिक दायित्व भएको उल्लेख गर्दै सडक बालबालिका मुक्त नेपाल बनाउने राष्ट्रिय लक्ष्य हासिल गर्न मन्त्रालय दृढतापूर्वक अगाडि बढिरहेको बताइन ।

articles.title: रौतहटमा जीवितैलाई ‘विधवा’ र उमेर नपुग्दै ‘वृद्ध’ बनाएर भत्ता वितरण, वडा अध्यक्षसहित ४२ विरुद्ध मुद्दा
articles.summary:
रौतहटको दुर्गा भगवती गाउँपालिका-३ मा सामाजिक सुरक्षा भत्ता वितरणमा व्यापक भ्रष्टाचार गरेको अभियोगमा अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले वडा अध्यक्ष र तत्कालीन निमित्त कार्यकारी अधिकृतसहित ४२ जना विरुद्ध विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ।

उमेरै नपुगेका व्यक्तिलाई ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र श्रीमान् जीवितै रहेका महिलालाई एकल महिला/विधवा भत्ता बाँडेर सरकारी रकम हिनामिना गरेको पुष्टि भएपछि आयोगले आइतबार आरोपपत्र दायर गरेको हो।

अख्तियारले वडा नं-३ का वडा अध्यक्ष धर्मेन्द्र कुमार झा र वडा सचिव उमेश चौधरीविरुद्ध जनही ३२ लाख २४ हजार १ रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबी गरेको छ।

यस्तै, गाउँपालिकाका तत्कालीन निमित्त कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रमोद कुमार ठाकुरविरुद्ध २९ लाख ४४ हजार १ रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबीसहित मुद्दा दायर गरिएको छ। अन्य प्रतिवादीहरूमा गैरकानुनी रूपमा भत्ता लिने स्थानीय र तिनका हकवालाहरू रहेका छन्।

अनुसन्धानका क्रममा वडा कार्यालयले बैंकिङ प्रणाली लागू हुनुपूर्व र लागू भएपछि समेत आपसी मिलेमतोमा आवश्यक कागजात बिना नै गैरकानुनी रूपमा जेष्ठ नागरिक र विधवा भत्ता वितरण गरेको पाइएको छ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०७४/०७५ देखि २०८१/०८२ सम्म योग्यता नपुगेका व्यक्तिहरूलाई सरकारी अभिलेखमा लाभार्थी कायम गरी दोहोरो स्रेस्ता खडा गरेर रकम हिनामिना गरिएको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ।

अख्तियारका प्रवक्ता सुरेश न्यौपानेका अनुसार वडा कार्यालयले नियमविपरीत सामाजिक सुरक्षा भत्ता व्यवस्थापन सूचना प्रणालीमा समेत झुटा विवरण प्रविष्टि गरी कुल ३२ लाख २४ हजार १ रुपैयाँ बराबरको सार्वजनिक सम्पत्ति हानि-नोक्सानी गरेको पुष्टि भएको छ।

भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन, २०५९ को दफा १७, ९ र ११ बमोजिम कसुर पुष्टि भएकाले प्रतिवादीहरूबाट बिगो असुलउपर गरी जरिवाना र कैद सजायको मागदाबीसहित विशेष अदालत काठमाडौंमा मुद्दा दायर गरिएको आयोगले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: नुवाकोटको पहिरो प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा राहत र पुनःस्थापनाका लागि पहल
articles.summary:
अविरल वर्षाका कारण नुवाकोटका विभिन्न क्षेत्रमा पहिरो तथा वर्षाजन्य विपद्का घटना बढ्दै गएपछि नुवाकोट-१ का प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य एवं सूचना तथा सञ्चारमन्त्री डा विक्रम तिमिल्सिनाले प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा तत्काल उद्धार, राहत तथा पुनःस्थापनाका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग तीव्र समन्वय र पहल अघि बढाएका छन् ।

जिल्लाको दुप्चेश्वर गाउँपालिका, सूर्यगढी गाउँपालिका, तादी गाउँपालिका, पञ्चकन्या गाउँपालिकालगायत क्षेत्रमा पहिरो र वर्षाजन्य विपद्का घटना भएका जानकारी प्राप्त भएपछि मन्त्री तिमिल्सिनाले प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी, जिल्ला प्रहरी प्रमुख तथा सम्बन्धित सरकारी निकायका प्रतिनिधिहरूसँग तत्काल समन्वय गरी प्रभावित क्षेत्रको अवस्थाबारे जानकारी लिएका हुन् ।

उनले घटनास्थलको स्थलगत अनुगमन, नागरिकको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चितता, आवश्यक उद्धार तथा राहत कार्यलाई प्रभावकारी रूपमा सञ्चालन गर्न र क्षतिको यथार्थ विवरण सङ्कलन गर्न सम्बन्धित निकायलाई आग्रह गरे। सञ्चारमन्त्री डा तिमिल्सिनाले राष्ट्रिय विपद् जोखिम न्यूनीकरण तथा व्यवस्थापन प्राधिकरण, जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय, सुरक्षा निकाय तथा अन्य सम्बन्धित निकायसँग निरन्तर सम्पर्क र समन्वय गरिरहनुभएको उहाँको सचिवालयले जनाएको छ ।

त्यसैगरी दुप्चेश्वर, सूर्यगढी तथा पञ्चकन्या गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष एवं स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधिसँग प्रत्यक्ष संवाद गरी घटनास्थलको वस्तुस्थिति बुझ्ने, तत्काल आवश्यक सहयोगको व्यवस्थापन गर्ने तथा राहत, पुनस्र्थापना र पुनर्निर्माणका कार्यलाई प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढाउने विषयमा आवश्यक समन्वय भइरहेको सचिवालयले जनाएको छ ।

यसैबीच, डा तिमिल्सिनाले सडक डिभिजन कार्यालय, नुवाकोटका प्रमुख इञ्जिनियर बद्री शर्मासँग मन्त्रालयमा भेट गरी अविरल वर्षाका कारण सडक, यातायात तथा अन्य पूर्वाधारमा पुगेको क्षतिबारे जानकारी लिए । भेटका क्रममा उनले अवरुद्ध सडक यथाशीघ्र सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन, प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा उद्धार तथा राहत कार्यमा सहज पहुँच सुनिश्चित गर्न र आवश्यक मर्मत तथा पुनःस्थापनाका कामलाई प्राथमिकताका साथ तीव्र गतिमा अघि बढाउन निर्देशन दिएको सचिवालयले जनाएको छ ।

सञ्चारमन्त्रीले प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीसँग पनि प्रत्यक्ष सम्पर्क गरी प्रभावित क्षेत्रको पछिल्लो अवस्थाबारे जानकारी लिँदै उद्धार, राहत, सडक सञ्चालन तथा अन्य अत्यावश्यक सेवाहरूलाई शीघ्र नियमित सञ्चालन गराउन आवश्यक समन्वय भइरहेको बताए । आवश्यकता अनुसार थप हस्तक्षेप तथा सहयोगका उपायबारे सम्बन्धित निकायसँग निरन्तर छलफल गरिने मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ ।

हाल सम्बन्धित निकायहरू प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा परिचालित भई उद्धार, राहत वितरण, क्षतिको विवरण सङ्कलन तथा अन्य आवश्यक कार्यमा सक्रिय रूपमा खटिएका जनाइएको छ । प्राप्त विवरणका आधारमा प्रभावित क्षेत्रका समस्याको दीर्घकालीन तथा दिगो समाधानका लागि आवश्यक अध्ययन, समन्वय तथा पहलसमेत अघि बढाइने सञ्चारमन्त्री डा तिमिल्सिनाको सचिवालयले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: संसदमा प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग प्रश्नोत्तर कहिले ?
articles.summary:
प्रतिनिधिसभा नियमावली, २०८३ कार्यान्वयनमा आएसँगै मन्त्रीहरूले संसद्मा नियमित प्रश्नोत्तरमा सहभागी हुन थाले पनि प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहले भने हालसम्म संसद्मा औपचारिक प्रश्नोत्तर सामना गरेका छैनन्।

प्रतिनिधिसभा नियमावलीको व्यवस्था अनुसार प्रधानमन्त्री वा प्रधानमन्त्रीको कार्यक्षेत्रसँग प्रत्यक्ष सम्बन्धित महत्वपूर्ण विषयमा सभामुखले प्रत्येक महिनाको पहिलो हप्ताको कुनै एक दिनको बैठकको पहिलो एक घण्टा प्रश्नोत्तरका लागि निर्धारण गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था छ। यही व्यवस्थाअनुसार प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग सांसदहरूले प्रत्यक्ष प्रश्न गर्न पाउनेछन्।

असार ३१ गते बसेको प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठक साउन १४ गतेसम्मका लागि स्थगित भएकाले अब बस्ने बैठकमा प्रश्नोत्तर कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन हुने सम्भावना छ। नयाँ नियमावली असार १८ गते प्रतिनिधिसभाबाट पारित भएको थियो।

यसअघि असार १७ गते प्रधानमन्त्री शाह आकस्मिक रूपमा संसद् बैठकमा उपस्थित भएर सांसदहरूले उठाएका प्रश्नको जवाफ दिएका थिए। भारतसँग सम्बन्धित अभिव्यक्तिलाई लिएर विपक्षी दलहरूले आलोचना गरेपछि प्रधानमन्त्रीले त्यसबारे स्पष्ट पारेका थिए। तर त्यो औपचारिक प्रश्नोत्तर कार्यक्रम भने थिएन।

प्रधानमन्त्री नियुक्त भएयता साढे तीन महिनाको अवधिमा शाह सात पटक प्रतिनिधिसभा बैठकमा उपस्थित भएका छन्। संसद् सचिवालयका अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार विगतका प्रधानमन्त्रीहरू पनि नियमित रूपमा संसद्मा उपस्थित हुने अभ्यासमा सधैं देखिएका थिएनन्।

संसदीय व्यवस्थामा प्रधानमन्त्रीको संसद् उपस्थित र जवाफदेहिता महत्वपूर्ण विषय मानिन्छ। बेलायतमा प्रधानमन्त्रीले प्रत्येक साता सांसदका प्रश्नको सामना गर्ने अभ्यास रहेको छ भने भारतमा पनि संसद्को प्रश्नोत्तर समयमा प्रधानमन्त्रीको सहभागिता रहने गर्छ।

नेपालमा पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई संसद्प्रति थप उत्तरदायी बनाउने उद्देश्यले प्रश्नोत्तर प्रणाली राखिएको हो। अब प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले कहिलेदेखि यो व्यवस्थालाई नियमित रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्छन् भन्ने विषयमा चासो बढेको छ।

articles.title: Paddy season is slipping away, but two Nepali farmer brothers are stuck in India jail
articles.summary:
Two farmers from Sarlahi district have spent nearly three weeks in an Indian prison after being arrested while returning home with chemical fertiliser bought from a border market. Their arrest is the latest reminder of Nepal’s chronic fertiliser shortages, which force many farmers to buy subsidised fertiliser across the border despite the legal risks.

Suresh Prasad Singh, 55, and his elder brother Nagendra Prasad Singh, 60, of ward 5 in Balara Municipality were detained on July 1 by a joint team of India's Agriculture Department and the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) near Sonbarsa in Bihar. According to their family members, the brothers had purchased two sacks of urea and six sacks of diammonium phosphate (DAP).

Instead of transplanting paddy on their roughly two-and-a-half bigha (1.69 hectares) of land, as they usually would by this time of year, the brothers remain behind bars at a jail in Dumra of Sitamarhi district. Their fields have been left uncultivated as the monsoon planting season advances.

Family members insist that the fertiliser was intended solely for use on their own farm and reject allegations of smuggling.

Prabin Singh, Nagendra's son-in-law, said the legal process has moved slowly despite repeated efforts by relatives. "The court sought documents related to the case from Sonbarsa police, but the bail hearing has yet to be completed," he said. "We have been told that the judge was on leave. We hope they will be released after a hearing this week, but the delay has caused enormous anxiety for the family."

According to relatives, all necessary paperwork has already reached the court, yet procedural delays have prolonged the brothers’ detention.

The arrest has placed the family under severe financial and emotional distress. Farming is their main source of income, but the land remains uncultivated because the two brothers, who normally manage cultivation, are still in custody.

"Our neighbours have already finished planting paddy, but our land is still lying fallow," said Aditya Singh, Suresh's son. "We are waiting for them to come home so that we can begin cultivation."

District officials in Nepal say they have been coordinating with Indian authorities, although they acknowledge that the judicial process lies beyond their control.

Hom Prasad Ghimire, assistant chief district officer of Sarlahi, said local officials have remained in contact with Indian security agencies regarding the case.

"We are continuing coordination for their release and are awaiting the latest update," he said.

Chief District Officer Bijay Raj Subedi said the Home Ministry had already been informed about the arrest and that local authorities were also communicating with the SSB.

"We have ensured that the family members have been able to meet them and that they are receiving the treatment and access they are entitled to during the legal process," said Subedi. "Further initiatives are being handled at higher levels." He added that Indian officials had informally explained that subsidised fertiliser is intended exclusively for Indian farmers and that security agencies have been instructed to prevent its movement across the international border.

Under India's Fertiliser (Control) Order and the Essential Commodities Act 1955 subsidised fertiliser distributed for agricultural use cannot legally be exported or transported outside the country without authorisation. Violations may result in confiscation of both the fertiliser and the vehicle used for transportation, while offenders can face imprisonment and fines

The case has again exposed the annual fertiliser crisis that affects farmers across the country, mainly in the southern plains considered as granary of Nepal. Every planting season, long queues form outside government depots operated by the Agriculture Inputs Company and local authorities as farmers compete for limited stocks of subsidised fertiliser.

Many farmers complain that supplies often arrive late or run out before demand is met. As a result, purchasing fertiliser from nearby Indian markets and carrying it home on bicycles or on foot has become common practice in many border communities despite the legal risks involved.

Local people of Balara claim that the Singh brothers are the latest victims of a problem rooted in shortages rather than criminal intent. Neighbour Anirudh Singh said the government should intensify diplomatic and legal efforts for their release.

"They are genuine farmers, not smugglers," said Anirudh. "They crossed the border only because they couldn’t get enough fertiliser at home. The government should do everything possible to bring them back."

Mohna Ansari, former National Human Rights Commission member, described the incident as deeply troubling. "It is unfortunate that farmers searching for an essential agricultural input have ended up in a foreign prison," she said. "The government should formally seek clarification through diplomatic channels about why its citizens have been detained and ensure the case is addressed without unnecessary delay."

She said both the Home Ministry and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs should actively engage with their Indian counterparts if the brothers are detained for transporting fertiliser intended for their own farm.

articles.title: Chief Minister Shah weighs confidence vote as Sudurpashchim sinks deeper into budget crisis
articles.summary:
Sudurpashchim Province is grappling with twin crises after the provincial government failed to endorse the budget for the new fiscal year, and Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah lost his majority when the CPN-UML withdrew support from the ruling coalition.

The political uncertainty has fuelled debate over whether Shah should resign or seek a vote of confidence in the Provincial Assembly within the 30-day constitutional deadline. The prolonged deadlock has also raised concerns over how long the province can function without a budget.

The Nepali Congress-led coalition, which included the UML, tabled the budget for the next fiscal year in the Provincial Assembly on June 15 with the backing of ministers from both parties. The alliance unravelled after the UML rejected the budget and registered a proposal to cut the allocations of six ministries to a token Re1 each.

Shah responded by dismissing four UML ministers, including a minister of state, on July 15. The UML then formally withdrew its support, leaving the government in a minority. The opposition Nepali Communist Party (NCP) immediately demanded that Shah resign to make way for a new administration.

Shah, however, has ruled out stepping down for now, saying he is awaiting the outcome of discussions among senior leaders in Kathmandu.

“There is no need to rush. The constitution provides a 30-day window,” Shah told the Post. “Talks are under way among the top leaders at the centre, and I believe a solution will emerge.”

Under the constitution, a chief minister must seek a vote of confidence within 30 days if a coalition partner withdraws support or if a no-confidence motion is registered.

“Rather than resigning, I will test my majority on the floor of the assembly in line with the constitution,” Shah said. “We are also holding discussions with various political parties in the province.”

Before the coalition collapsed, the government commanded 29 seats, with 18 lawmakers from the Nepali Congress and 11 from the UML. In the 53-member Provincial Assembly, 27 seats are required for a majority.

With the alliance broken, the NCP has become the key player. The party holds 20 seats, excluding the Speaker and one suspended lawmaker. The assembly also has one member from the Rastriya Prajatantra Party, while one seat is vacant.

Any new government will require an alliance between at least two of the three largest parties, the NCP, Congress and UML. Congress president Gagan Thapa has already said his party will not support a three-party coalition in the province.

After losing UML backing, Shah sought support from the NCP, but the party has remained firm that he must first resign.

“Since the chief minister has lost his majority, our parliamentary party has decided that he should resign to pave the way for a new government,” said Khag Raj Bhatta, leader of the NCP parliamentary party. “We have already resolved to take the initiative to form a government under our leadership.”

The political impasse has also pushed the province into a fiscal crisis. With no alternative arrangement made before the end of the previous fiscal year, Sudurpashchim entered a financial vacuum on July 17.

It is the second such crisis in the province. Political disputes last year also left Sudurpashchim without a budget for three months.

Without an approved budget, government agencies cannot authorise public spending. Shah said the government is considering introducing an ordinance to allow advance expenditure. According to him, the executive still has the authority to bring a bill for revenue collection and meet administrative and operational expenses.

Although the fiscal vacuum has halted government spending, revenue collection and essential public services will continue. In the absence of a Financial Act, revenue will be collected under the Provisional Revenue Collection Act.

Chakra Bahadur Malla, the UML chief whip in the province, blamed Shah entirely for the crisis.

“The chief minister made no effort from June 15 to July 15. We had made it clear immediately after the budget was presented that we would not support it,” Malla said. “Had he initiated dialogue earlier, we could have reconsidered the issues affecting the province.”

Civil society leaders have criticised the repeated fiscal paralysis, calling it a reflection of political irresponsibility.

“This provincial government has shown no signs of improvement. Political leaders have treated the province like a toy,” said Pramod Pathak, a civil society activist in Dhangadhi. “We hear nothing but stories of mismanagement. Failing to pass the budget on time raises serious questions about the relevance of the provincial structure.”

articles.title: १७ लाख ठगेको आरोपमा पूजा माइतीघरबाट पक्राउ
articles.summary:
वैदेशिक रोजगारीका लागि बेलायत (युके) पठाइदिने प्रलोभन देखाएर १७ लाख रुपैयाँ ठगी गरेको आरोपमा एक महिला पक्राउ परेकी छिन्।

काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका-१७ बस्ने ३२ वर्षीया पूजा शाहीलाई काठमाडौंको माइतीघरबाट पक्राउ गरिएको हो। वैदेशिक रोजगार विभागबाट जारी भएको पक्राउ पुर्जीका आधारमा उनलाई नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

शाहीमाथि एक जना पीडितसँग बेलायत पठाइदिने भन्दै १७ लाख रुपैयाँ लिई सम्पर्कविहीन भएर ठगी गरेको आरोप रहेको छ। उनीमाथि आवश्यक थप अनुसन्धान भइरहेको प्रहरीले जानकारी दिएको छ।

articles.title: बैतडीको गोकुलेश्वरमा सबैभन्दा बढी वर्षा
articles.summary:
पछिल्लो तीन घण्टामा देशभरमै सबैभन्दा बढी वर्षा बैतडीको गोकुलेश्वरमा मापन गरिएको छ। जल तथा मौसम विज्ञान विभागका अनुसार गोकुलेश्वरमा ३७.२ मिलिमिटर वर्षा भएको छ।

विभागले जारी गरेको पछिल्लो मौसम बुलेटिनअनुसार गोकुलेश्वर क्षेत्रमा छोटो अवधिमै ठूलो वर्षा भएको हो। हाल मनसुन सक्रिय रहेकाले देशभरकै मौसममा बदली भई विभिन्न स्थानमा वर्षा भइरहेको विभागले जनाएको छ।

हाल कोसी, वागमती, लुम्बिनी र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशका थोरै स्थानहरूमा हल्कादेखि मध्यम वर्षा भइरहेको छ। यसैगरी मधेस, गण्डकी र कर्णाली प्रदेशका एक-दुई स्थानमा पनि मौसम बदली भई हल्का वर्षा भइरहेको छ।

देशभरका विभिन्न भू-भागमा वर्षा भइरहेकाले पहाडी क्षेत्रमा पहिरो तथा गेग्रान बहावको जोखिम रहेको र नदीनालाहरूमा पानीको बहाव बढ्न सक्ने भएकाले आवश्यक सतर्कता अपनाउन विभागले सर्वसाधारणलाई आग्रह गरेको छ।
